en.heading: Game Overview
en.body: Game Overview Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for publisher/platform/current feature names; community-verified for deeper mechanics. Dark War: Survival is a mobile strategy game published by Florere Game Limited . The official store description frames the game around rebuilding a shelter after a zombie-virus collapse, developing survivors and troops, joining alliances, and competing on a shared world map. Core gameplay loop The long-term game loop combines several systems rather than a single progression track: 1. Shelter development — upgrade the Watchtower and prerequisite buildings, maintain resource production, research technology and train units. 2. Hero development — recruit heroes, raise levels and stars, improve skills and equipment, and build formations around faction synergy. 3. Troop development — train Fighter, Rider and Shooter units and unlock higher tiers as the shelter progresses. 4. APC / Modified Vehicle development — improve the vehicle, parts and chips that support formations on the world map. 5. Alliance play — rallies, alliance research, territory activity, alliance events and cross-state competition are major sources of progress and rewards. 6. Seasonal systems — seasons add temporary buildings, resistance mechanics, currencies, monsters and territory objectives. 7. Recurring events — progression resources are frequently tied to timed events such as Alliance Duel, Survival Preparedness, State of Supremacy, Zombie Siege and Bio-Mutant. Current-era systems worth knowing Official patch notes confirm that the game has continued to expand well beyond the original launch systems. Examples include: - Industrial Age progression beyond the normal Watchtower era. - Modified Vehicle parts, chips, set bonuses and Tactical Modification. - Wonders the feature previously called Decorations and Wonder Gallery management. - Pet Agents / Special Ops Outpost , including rescue, training and growth systems. - Fierce March , a VIP 12 command that can automatically engage enemy troops encountered along a march path. Because systems change over time, Server 504 Wiki should prefer dated patch information for hard limits and unlock conditions instead of treating old community tables as permanent truth. Publisher and platform - Publisher / developer shown by the major app stores: Florere Game Limited . - Category: Strategy . - Free-to-play with in-app purchases. - The global Google Play listing has exceeded 10 million downloads . Wiki policy This Wiki documents Dark War: Survival only . Information from unrelated games with similar UI, advertising style or genre must not be used as a substitute source. en.heading: Combat System & Reports
en.body: Combat System & Battle Reports Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for current world-battle/report behavior; medium for community-tested damage-engine details. Dark War: Survival uses the same account investments across several battle modes, but the way those investments are expressed is not identical in every fight. For practical planning, separate troop battles from hero-battle / Adventure-style combat . Troop battles Troop battles are the main reference for server warfare. They include world-map PvP, shelter attacks and defenses, rallies, many alliance fights and other engagements that generate a battle report. A battle report is more useful than the win/loss banner because it can expose the actual sources behind a formation's strength, including: - troop count and remaining troops; - hero contribution; - Hero Equipment; - technologies; - Modified Vehicle / APC bonuses; - faction-related bonuses; - combat rounds and skill activations. Community battle-log testing shows that troop combat combines many percentage bonuses into a shared formation-level combat pool. This is why a lower displayed CP formation can sometimes perform better when its faction research, hero passives and vehicle bonuses are better aligned. Hero battles / Adventure combat Adventure-style encounters visibly resolve around individual heroes. Community testing distinguishes front-line defensive roles from back-line damage roles and reports that individual hero stats and gear allocation matter more directly here than in troop battles. The precise hidden formulas are not officially published, so Server 504 Wiki should treat exact damage formulas as community-tested , not official constants. How to use reports for improvement When reviewing a loss, check the gap in this order: 1. Troop tier and troop count — an undersized formation loses output and durability quickly. 2. Faction matchup — Fighter, Rider and Shooter counters can change an otherwise close fight. 3. Hero passives / formation buffs — these often scale the whole troop rather than one hero. 4. Research — especially primary-faction ATK/DEF/HP/damage research. 5. Hero Equipment — compare the actual report contribution, not only equipment CP. 6. Modified Vehicle and chips — late-game vehicle bonuses can be one of the largest report lines. 7. Season, alliance, wonder, skin and other account-wide bonuses . Damage-cycle caution Several community test reports describe a repeating normal-attack / skill-activation cycle and show skills firing at predictable round intervals. Because the developer does not publish the complete combat formula, the Wiki should not present reverse-engineered round formulas as guaranteed behavior without a current Server 504 report to verify them. Server 504 evidence standard For future combat-formula articles, preserve screenshots of: - the troop overview; - Troop Buffs pages; - Hero Equipment comparison; - round-by-round log; - attacker and defender formation composition. This allows formulas to be re-tested after patches instead of relying on old guides. en.heading: Factions & Heroes
en.body: Factions & Heroes Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for faction structure; medium for hero-specific values because balance data can change. Heroes and troops in Dark War: Survival are organized around three combat factions: - Fighter - Rider - Shooter Community reference data consistently describes a counter triangle: Faction Strong against Weak against --- --- --- Fighter Rider Shooter Rider Shooter Fighter Shooter Fighter Rider Same-faction formations are important because faction bonuses, research, chips and hero passives can multiply the same troop type. For most players, concentrating investment into one primary faction produces a stronger main formation than spreading early resources evenly across all three. Hero progression A hero's practical strength comes from several layers: 1. Level — raises base hero attributes. 2. Stars / fragments — improves skills and progression bonuses. 3. Skills — active, normal attack and progression-oriented skills vary by hero. 4. Standard equipment — provides combat attributes and can be enhanced/upgraded. 5. Exclusive Equipment — hero-specific equipment that can add unique skills and additional attributes. 6. Formation context — faction match, troop type, front/back position and the rest of the team matter as much as isolated hero CP. Formation principle For a developing account, a useful default is: - choose one primary faction; - focus the strongest five heroes that support that formation; - align troop research and APC/chip investment with that faction; - build a second formation only after the main one has a solid equipment and research base. This is a strategy guideline rather than a fixed game rule. Specific heroes can justify mixed lineups when their skills are strong enough. Hero data policy Hero-specific skill numbers are especially vulnerable to balance changes. The Server 504 Wiki should therefore store hero pages with: - hero name; - rarity/class; - faction; - role/specialty; - acquisition source; - active and passive skill descriptions; - exclusive equipment, if available; - last verified date ; - source screenshot or current data reference when possible. Avoid copying an old tier list as permanent truth. Tier strength changes with new heroes, Exclusive Equipment, Industrial progression, chips and seasonal mechanics. Until the Server 504 hero index or a clean independent current source resolves this, the Wiki should not silently pick one. Conflict queue Katrina / Katerina spelling Community databases consistently use Katrina , while an official 2025 patch note refers to Katerina when mentioning an Exclusive Equipment animation optimization alongside Darian. Both his Adventure food/energy passive and combat use are real, so the database leaves the formal type label unresolved rather than discarding one side of the evidence. Several provide long-term account utility: - Quinn — unit training / Alliance Duel progression value; - Corleone — research economy and speed; - Megan — construction economy and speed; - Evans — Modified Vehicle / Gear progression; - Catherine & Rex — Radar progression; - Guy — Adventure food and energy utility. Exclusive Equipment rule Official patch notes state that the Hero Exclusive Weapon / Exclusive Equipment system: - unlocks after the State has progressed for a required period; - applies to Orange-quality heroes ; - opens the hero's Exclusive Equipment slot at 2 Stars ; - adds troop damage, troop HP and stronger faction-counter effects; - unlocks an additional special combat skill. Later official updates added Red Star breakthrough, Hall of Honor progression and star-level swapping between Red Star Exclusive Equipment using a Core of Rotation . Because Exclusive Equipment can materially change a hero's value, the Wiki must keep hero identity data separate from current investment ranking . Individual profile status The current public S-rarity roster now has individual pages for all verified entries, plus a verification-pending page for Lan Yan. Each page keeps stable identity and skill data separate from fast-changing investment advice. en.heading: Hero Investment Framework
en.body: Hero Investment Framework Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Purpose: Separate stable hero data from fast-changing meta recommendations. A permanent tier list is a poor fit for Dark War: Survival because hero value changes with: - State age and hero generation; - faction research depth; - star level and fragment availability; - standard equipment quality; - Exclusive Equipment availability and breakthrough; - APC/chip alignment; - the player's existing investment; - PvP, boss, Adventure or progression goals. The Server 504 Wiki therefore uses an investment framework instead of treating one public tier list as universal truth. 1. Decide whether the hero is Combat or Progression-first Combat-first examples Examples in the current S-rarity dataset include: - Tristan, Francis, Noah; - Cyrus, Marcia, Katrina, Lucas; - Natasha, Margaret, Darian, Rosa. These heroes should primarily be evaluated against the player's main faction, formation role, stars, equipment and Exclusive Equipment. Progression-first examples - Quinn — training and Alliance Duel value; - Corleone — research value; - Megan — construction value; - Evans — Modified Vehicle progression; - Catherine & Rex — Radar progression; - Guy — Adventure food / energy value. A progression hero can remain worth starring even if they are no longer a top PvP slot. 2. Main faction comes before isolated hero popularity A strong hero from the wrong faction may add less account value than a slightly weaker hero who multiplies the player's existing: - troop research; - faction passives; - troop tier investment; - APC chips; - equipment plan; - formation presets. For most accounts, deep investment into one primary faction produces better results than repeatedly switching because a new hero appears on a tier list. 3. Compare replacement cost, not just theoretical strength Before replacing an established hero, compare: - current star difference; - fragment availability; - skill investment; - equipment already assigned; - Exclusive Equipment investment; - whether the new hero requires changing faction or formation structure. A newer hero can be stronger at equal development while still being a poor immediate investment for a mature account. 4. Exclusive Equipment can change the answer Official patch notes confirm that Exclusive Equipment is available to Orange-quality heroes once the State reaches the required progression age and the hero reaches 2 Stars. Exclusive Equipment adds combat attributes and a special combat skill. Later systems added Red Star breakthrough, Hall of Honor progression and star-level swapping between Red Star Exclusive Equipment. Therefore every future meta assessment should have two separate fields: - Without Exclusive Equipment - With current Exclusive Equipment state Do not rank a hero as if these two states were equivalent. 5. Hero Battle role is separate from faction Community testing describes Hero Battles / Adventure as having role behavior beyond faction labels. Tanker-type heroes provide frontline survival while Striker-type heroes provide sustained damage between skill rounds. This means a formation can fail even when the faction is correct if the frontline/backline function is poor. For individual hero pages, the Wiki should eventually record the current in-game role icon separately from faction and specialty. 6. Use a decision label instead of a permanent tier Recommended labels for Server 504: - Core now — currently important to the player's main formation; - Build if switching — strong candidate when moving into that faction; - Progression utility — worth building for economy/event value; - Keep invested — older hero still efficient because existing stars/equipment are high; - Replace only after breakpoint — new hero becomes efficient only after reaching a defined star/equipment threshold; - Verification pending — public sources disagree or current Server 504 data is missing. These labels are more actionable than S+ / S / A without context. 7. Update cadence Stable fields such as name, faction and specialty should change rarely. Meta fields should carry their own date: - identity verified at - skills verified at - exclusive equipment verified at - meta reviewed at This prevents an old recommendation from making the entire hero profile look current. Official hero-system changes that matter to ranking Official version history confirms several changes that make old hero guides risky to copy directly: - hero skills and faction systems have been reworked over time; - Exclusive Equipment was added for Orange heroes; - Red Star and Hall of Honor systems were added later; - lower-rarity Blue/Purple Exclusive Talents were rebalanced in 2025; - hero index now includes season labels; - Exclusive Equipment visuals and systems continue to receive updates. Sources - Apple App Store — Dark War: Survival version history: - DarkWarData — hero database: - Dark War Survival Guide — Hero Battles: - Meta Instincts community guide — Hero system update:

en.heading: Quinn
en.body: Quinn Identity verified: 7 Aug 2026 Meta reviewed: 7 Aug 2026 Rarity: S / Orange Faction: Rider Specialty: Alliance Duel / unit training progression Quinn is a Rider hero whose long-term value comes from account progression and Alliance Duel scoring , not only direct combat. Acquisition Community data lists Quinn as recruitable through the Radio Station . Skill structure Devastator's Blade — Active Skill Direct-damage Active Skill following the standard S-rarity skill pattern. Swordsmanship — Normal Attack Standard Normal Attack progression. Butcher Instructor — Progression Skill This is the defining part of Quinn's profile. Public data lists: - reduced basic resource cost for unit training; - increasing unit training speed as stars rise; - increasing Alliance Duel points as stars rise; - at the highest listed star breakpoint, a very large training-speed increase and +50% Alliance Duel points . Exact current values should still be checked in Server 504 before using them in a scoring calculator. High Morale — Exclusive Talent Public data lists hero ATK +10%, DEF +10% and troop capacity +5%. Current usefulness Decision label: Progression utility / keep invested. Quinn is a strong example of why the Wiki does not rank every hero only by PvP damage. Even if a different Rider replaces her in a main combat formation, her unit-training and Alliance Duel value can justify continued investment. Best-fit use cases: - Alliance Duel preparation; - unit-training days; - accounts trying to increase score efficiency per saved training resource; - secondary Rider formation when combat stats are sufficient. Exclusive Equipment Quinn is Orange quality and therefore belongs to the hero quality eligible for the game's Exclusive Equipment system once the State and hero-star requirements are met. Her hero-specific Exclusive Equipment details still require current in-game capture before the Wiki publishes a definitive effect table. en.heading: Hero Skills & Passives
en.body: Hero Skills & Passives Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for the skill categories shown on established hero data; medium for individual values because heroes are patched over time. Hero value in Dark War: Survival is not determined by displayed CP alone. A hero can contribute direct damage, faction-wide combat buffs, troop capacity, economy, training, research or event scoring depending on the skill set. Common skill structure Established hero databases repeatedly show four broad skill/talent layers on heroes: 1. Active Skill — the hero's main combat skill. 2. Normal Attack — repeated direct damage between major skill activations. 3. Passive / Progression Skill — varies widely by hero. It may buff a faction, improve training/research/resources, increase event scoring or support another account system. 4. Exclusive Talent — an additional hero/faction-oriented attribute layer. The third slot is especially important to read carefully. It is not always a combat passive. For example, some heroes improve faction ATK/DEF/HP or battle damage while others specialize in training, research, gathering or Alliance Duel progression. Faction passives Combat heroes can provide bonuses to Fighter, Rider or Shooter troops. These bonuses are valuable because they can scale an entire formation rather than only the hero that owns the skill. Examples documented by community databases include heroes whose passives increase: - faction ATK; - faction DEF; - faction HP; - battle damage; - normal-attack damage reduction; - skill damage; - troop capacity. Exact percentages should live on individual hero pages with a verification date. Blue and purple hero talent update Official September 2025 patch notes changed several lower-rarity heroes' exclusive talents so they remain relevant in developed accounts. The update added effects such as: - troop capacity increases; - ATK for in-troop Fighter / Shooter / Rider heroes; - DEF for in-troop Fighter / Shooter / Rider heroes. This confirms an important Wiki rule: rarity alone does not tell the whole story, and old hero descriptions can become obsolete after talent reworks. Upgrade priority Do not use a universal rule such as “always max Active first” for every hero. A better process is: 1. identify the hero's real job in the formation; 2. determine whether the key value is combat, faction support or progression utility; 3. compare the next skill level to the resource cost; 4. prioritize the main formation before secondary heroes; 5. re-check after unlocking Exclusive Equipment, because it can change a hero's practical value. Individual hero page standard Each future hero article should record: - faction and rarity; - combat/progression specialty; - Active Skill; - Normal Attack; - Passive/Progression Skill; - Exclusive Talent; - Exclusive Equipment, if available; - acquisition sources; - season/release context; - last verified date. Sources - Apple App Store version history — hero talent reworks and current hero-system changes: - Dark War Survival Data — hero database: Retired community hero-category links are intentionally excluded from current source authority.

en.heading: Hero Equipment
en.body: Hero Equipment Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for Power Core usage and equipment progression concepts; medium for exact stat values and shop availability. Hero equipment is a major combat-power layer in Dark War: Survival and should be developed together with the hero and formation rather than treated as cosmetic gear. Standard equipment Standard hero equipment provides combat attributes such as attack, defense, HP and troop-related bonuses. Equipment quality progresses through multiple rarity tiers, with Orange equipment serving as the key long-term baseline in older and current community guides. A practical development rule is to prioritize the main formation before spreading high-quality gear across many secondary heroes. Enhancement vs. upgrade Two progression ideas should be kept separate: - Enhancement raises equipment performance using enhancement materials or consumed equipment. - Upgrade / star progression uses rarer materials and becomes available on high-quality equipment after reaching the required enhancement level. The in-game description of Power Core explicitly states that it is used to upgrade hero equipment and that Orange equipment can be upgraded after it has been enhanced to Lv.20 . Power Cores Power Cores are a scarce progression material. Community data lists recurring sources such as: - Season Shop - VIP Shop - legacy Capital / Arena / Black Gold shop families now represented by the current Honor system where applicable - Trial Shop - selected event rewards - Bio-Mutant damage rewards - paid offers Shop contents and event thresholds can change, so the Wiki should verify current availability before publishing exact purchase priorities. Exclusive Equipment Exclusive Equipment is separate from standard equipment and is tied to specific heroes. It can provide: - additional hero-specific skills; - troop or faction attributes; - progression through its own star/breakthrough system. Official 2026 patch notes also confirm advanced Exclusive Equipment systems such as Red Star breakthrough and star-level swapping using a dedicated item. Practical priorities For most developing accounts: 1. fully equip the main formation before secondary formations; 2. use front-line gear to improve survivability and back-line gear to improve damage output; 3. avoid spending Power Cores without an equipment plan; 4. time expensive upgrades with scoring events when possible; 5. verify whether a hero's Exclusive Equipment materially changes the formation before investing heavily. Sources - Dark War Survival Data — Power Core: - Dark War Survival Data — Hero Equipment Lucky Chest: - Apple App Store version history: Retired community equipment-category links are intentionally excluded from current source authority.

en.heading: Exclusive Equipment & Hall of Honor
en.body: Exclusive Equipment & Hall of Honor Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for current Red Star / Swap / Hall of Honor behavior confirmed by official patch notes; medium for hero-specific effects and fragment costs. Exclusive Equipment is hero-specific progression that exists separately from standard Hero Equipment. It can add unique hero effects and additional troop or faction attributes, so unlocking it can materially change a hero's value. What is confirmed Official patches confirm that Exclusive Equipment has progressed beyond its original star system and now includes: - unlocking and upgrading hero-specific Exclusive Equipment; - breakthrough progression to Red Star ; - Hall of Honor progress associated with the equipment; - Exclusive Equipment Swap between eligible Red Star items; - the dedicated Core of Rotation item for a swap. When a swap succeeds, the two eligible Exclusive Equipment pieces exchange star levels and their Hall of Honor progress is swapped with them. Core of Rotation Official February 2026 notes state that each Exclusive Equipment Swap consumes 1 Core of Rotation . Because this is a specialized respec-like resource, it should not be treated as an ordinary upgrade material. Acquisition evolves over time Community guides from the feature's original release describe a much narrower set of Exclusive Equipment sources. Later official patches added Exclusive Equipment Fragments to the Daily Sale and introduced systems such as the Flea Market that can exchange surplus hero fragments for Exclusive Equipment fragments and other rare items. Therefore, old statements such as “this equipment is only obtainable from one paid pack” should not be copied into the Wiki without a date. Investment rule Before investing heavily, check: 1. Is the hero part of the current main formation? 2. Does the Exclusive Equipment add a formation-wide effect or mainly personal damage? 3. Is a newer-season hero likely to replace this hero soon? 4. Does the next breakthrough unlock a meaningful effect? 5. Would preserving fragments or a Core of Rotation offer more flexibility? What not to hard-code yet Fragment cost per star, breakthrough cost and hero-specific Exclusive Equipment effects should be stored per hero and verified against Server 504's current interface. These values are more likely to change than the general system structure. en.heading: Formations & Unit Presets
en.body: Formations & Unit Presets Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for current preset/defense features; medium for community formation-bonus math. Formation building in Dark War: Survival should align four layers: hero faction, troop faction, research and APC/chip setup . Fighter / Rider / Shooter The game supports three combat factions: - Fighter - Rider - Shooter The established counter triangle is: - Fighter counters Rider; - Rider counters Shooter; - Shooter counters Fighter. This means “highest CP” is not always the best answer when a faction counter or formation-wide passive is involved. Official Recommended presets Official October 2025 patch notes added a Recommended button to the troop interface with four one-tap schemes: - CP First - Fighter First - Shooter First - Rider First These are useful as a fast baseline, but they do not replace manual formation planning for PvP, rallies or specialized events. Defense Presets The same update introduced Defense Preset at the City Gate. Players can pre-set multiple defense squads. If heroes in the first preset are already deployed elsewhere, the game uses the next-priority preset. If no secondary preset exists, the strongest available heroes are auto-deployed. This makes defense planning important before large wars: a strong first lineup is not useful if its heroes are committed to another march when the shelter is hit. Same-faction concentration Community testing consistently recommends concentrating a main formation around one troop faction because the same investment can then be multiplied by: - faction research; - hero faction passives; - faction counter effects; - APC/chip bonuses; - formation/faction bonuses shown in combat reports. Some community guides report a same-faction formation bonus at specific hero counts. Because exact bonus values can be patched and are visible in reports, Server 504 Wiki should verify the current value in-game before publishing it as a permanent number. Chip-aware formations Official Chip System notes state that City Gate defense formations can intelligently match chip setups based on unit numbers and unit types . Later UI updates also added faction indicators to chip icons. Practical consequence: changing a formation's troop faction without checking its active chip setup can leave combat power on the table. Recommended planning workflow 1. Pick the target: world PvP, rally, defense, Adventure or event boss. 2. Check enemy faction if known. 3. Choose troop faction and hero core. 4. Confirm faction research supports that troop type. 5. Confirm APC/chip setup matches the formation. 6. Save separate Defense Presets for situations where the main march is away. 7. Compare battle reports after testing rather than trusting displayed CP alone. Sources - Apple App Store version history — Recommended presets, Defense Preset and chip-aware defense: - Dark War Survival community faction data: - Community formation testing:

en.heading: Rally, Reinforcement & Defense
en.body: Rally, Reinforcement & Defense Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for current Capital/Turret and Rally Restriction features; medium for situational community observations. Rallies and reinforcements are alliance-level combat tools. Their current behavior has changed through patches, so old “one rally only” or older capacity advice can be wrong. Rally A rally is an alliance attack initiated by one player and joined by other members. The initiator selects the target and can control rally restrictions when the feature is available. Official 2026 world-battle notes confirm Rally Restriction by unit type. The game also saves those restriction settings based on the troop, making faction-specific rally presets easier to reuse. Why restrictions matter If a rally strategy is built around Fighter, Rider or Shooter buffs, allowing every faction to join can weaken synergy. Restriction is therefore an operational tool, not merely a convenience setting. The exact combat contribution of the rally initiator versus joiners should be verified from battle reports before the Wiki publishes a universal “rally lead stats determine everything” rule. Community discussions often simplify this mechanic too aggressively. Capital and Turret changes Official December 2025 notes changed Capital/Turret warfare substantially: - rally limits for the Capital and Turrets were removed; - reinforcement limits for those targets were removed; - survivors can launch multiple rallies and send multiple reinforcement squads to the targets separately; - launching a rally or sending reinforcements to a Capital/Turret receives an additional 40,000 troop capacity . These rules supersede older guides written before that patch. Reinforcement Reinforcement sends a formation to defend another shelter or structure. It is used in alliance wars, Zombie Siege, territory defense and Capital/Turret control. Community observations report that reinforcement travel can be faster inside controlled alliance territory than across uncaptured territory. Treat this as a map/territory behavior to verify in the live server rather than a guaranteed fixed multiplier. City Gate defense Official updates added Defense Presets : - multiple defense squads can be prepared in advance; - if heroes in the first preset are busy, the next preset is used; - if no fallback preset exists, the strongest available heroes are auto-deployed. Before major combat, check that your defense formation is not accidentally dependent on heroes currently committed to a rally, gather or remote march. en.heading: Industrial Age & Precision Parts
en.body: Industrial Age & Precision Parts Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for the role of Precision Parts and the Industrial progression model; medium for exact Industrial-level costs because most numeric tables are community-maintained. Industrial progression begins after the normal level-30 building era and uses Precision Parts as a key bottleneck resource. What Precision Parts do Community databases consistently identify Precision Parts as the special material required to advance eligible buildings beyond normal level 30 into Industrial levels. Buildings commonly documented as Industrial-upgradeable include: - Watchtower; - Fighter Camp; - Rider Camp; - Shooter Camp; - Alliance Hall / Guild-related progression; - Hospital and other selected late-game structures depending on the current game version. Industrial upgrades are multi-step Community reports describe each Industrial level as a sequence of sub-upgrades rather than one instant jump. Players should therefore plan for repeated Precision Part spending before a building reaches the next displayed Industrial level. This is important when timing upgrades for Alliance Duel or Survival Preparedness: spending only part of the required sequence may score points without actually completing the next Industrial level. Community cost snapshot The following values are community-reported planning numbers , not official fixed costs. They are included because multiple independent reports broadly agree on the shape of the progression. Training camp progression One 2025 community report listed the following Precision Part requirements for a single faction camp: Camp progression Reported Precision Parts --- ---: Lv.30 → Industrial 1 400 total Industrial 1 → 2 450 total Industrial 2 → 3 550 total This implies approximately 1,400 Precision Parts to take one camp from normal Lv.30 to Industrial 3 under that version of the system. Watchtower minimum-path snapshots Community players have also reported minimum-path totals in which Watchtower upgrades require other Industrial prerequisites. Examples from 2025 reports include roughly: - Industrial 1: Watchtower path around 900 Precision Parts ; - Industrial 2: Watchtower + selected prerequisite structures around 1,750–1,800 total for that step; - Industrial 3: around 2,400 for that step; - later Industrial levels increase further. en.heading: Progression Planning
en.body: Progression Planning Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for planning principles; exact costs and unlocks remain versioned data. Efficient progression in Dark War: Survival is less about upgrading everything and more about keeping the next progression gate ready before the current one finishes. Core planning loop A practical progression cycle is: 1. identify the next Watchtower requirement; 2. pre-build its prerequisite while the current Watchtower upgrade is running; 3. keep the main faction camp and Battle research close enough to use the next troop milestone; 4. bank resources and speedups for the intended event window; 5. after WT30, replace normal-resource planning with a Precision Part / Industrial prerequisite plan. Early and mid-game bottlenecks Alliance Hall Alliance Hall appears repeatedly in higher Watchtower prerequisite chains and is one of the most common reasons a player reaches the next WT level but cannot start the following upgrade. Research Center Research Center acts as another periodic gate and should not be allowed to fall far behind. Even when it is not the immediate Watchtower prerequisite, troop research can still block the practical benefit of a new camp level. Resource transition Community progression tables agree that the resource burden broadens in the mid-game and rises sharply in the WT20+ range. Players approaching this point should stop thinking only in terms of the current upgrade and instead budget for a multi-level push. Event timing Construction resources have two values: - the permanent power/progression they buy; - the event points they can generate when spent at the right time. For Server 504 players, large Watchtower, Industrial and prerequisite upgrades should be checked against the current Alliance Duel and Survival Preparedness windows before using speedups or scarce materials. This does not mean every upgrade should be delayed. If delaying a progression gate costs days of troop/research growth, the lost account growth can be more expensive than the event points gained. Industrial planning Once Industrial progression begins: - Precision Parts become a hard planning resource; - one displayed Industrial level may require multiple sub-upgrades; - faction camps can compete with the Watchtower for the same scarce material; - broad upgrades are often weaker than completing the minimum prerequisite path for the next meaningful power milestone. A useful rule is to choose a primary combat faction before making expensive Industrial camp investments. What to record before an expensive push Before a major Watchtower or Industrial upgrade, record: - current Watchtower / Industrial level; - exact prerequisite buildings; - Precision Parts required; - raw resources required; - base build time shown; - active construction-cost reduction heroes or buffs; - current event scoring window; - expected troop or research unlock after completion. These screenshots can also feed back into the Server 504 Wiki so later players receive current-state data rather than old community estimates. Data policy The Wiki intentionally separates planning principles from hard-number tables . Planning principles remain useful across patches. Numeric tables must carry a verification date and should be replaced when Server 504 in-game evidence contradicts them. en.heading: APC & Modified Vehicle

Core progression layers The system has evolved over time and now contains several separate layers: - vehicle / modification level; - Modified Vehicle parts; - vehicle chips; - part set bonuses; - Tactical Modification; - vehicle skins and related bonuses. Older community references describe an earlier APC progression model with lower caps. These numbers should not be treated as current because official patch notes later expanded the system substantially. Important official changes Official October 2025 patch notes documented major expansion of Modified Vehicle progression: - the maximum Modify level was raised to 500 ; - upgrading six parts to specified levels can activate Parts Set bonuses and unlock skins; - part-upgrade resource requirements were changed; - vehicle chip progression became part of advanced unlock conditions; - Tactical Modification was introduced as an endgame layer. Tactical Modification can unlock when any one of several advanced conditions is met, including a high vehicle transformation level, sufficiently developed parts, or a highly starred Orange vehicle chip. Chips and formations Vehicle chips should be aligned with formation composition. Official patch notes confirm that the game can recommend troop setups by CP or faction and can intelligently match chip setups for defensive formations based on troop numbers and unit types. This reinforces a broader development rule: APC/chip investment should support the same primary faction being strengthened through troop research and hero development. en.heading: APC Chips
en.body: APC Chips Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for Chip System existence, official reward sources, star progression and formation integration; medium for exact crafting recipes. The Chip System is a later Modified Vehicle layer that lets survivors craft and install chips to increase APC combat power. Official launch behavior Official September 2025 patch notes introduced the Chip System and confirmed several recurring sources: - Chip Materials from the 3rd, 6th and 9th point-tier chests in Daily Alliance Duel; - Random Blue Chip Chests from Zombie Siege individual and alliance ranking rewards; - the Chip Chrono event; - later Mod Vehicle packs containing Purple or Green Chip Chests. Reward pools can change, so these are system/source references rather than a guaranteed permanent shopping list. Craft and install The developer explicitly describes the system as craft and install chips for the Modified Vehicle. However, public official notes do not document the full crafting recipe, menu unlock requirement or every rarity conversion step. For Server 504 Wiki, do not publish an old recipe as current truth unless it is verified from the current Chip Factory interface. Faction-aware chips Official updates show that chips are connected to troop composition: - Defense formations can automatically match the best chip setup based on unit numbers and unit types. - Later UI updates added faction indicators to chip icons. - Champion Duel fixes referenced chip bonuses syncing with formation changes. This means a chip setup should be treated as part of a formation, not as a separate “highest CP chip wins” system. Star progression Official patch notes refer directly to Chip star upgrades and later use an Orange vehicle chip reaching 10 stars as one of the unlock conditions for Tactical Modification. Therefore, chip progression has at least three strategically important layers: 1. chip rarity; 2. chip star level; 3. compatibility with the active formation/faction. Chip Factory data still needed To build a reliable crafting table, Server 504 should capture the current in-game Chip Factory and record: - exact unlock condition; - material names and quantities; - recipe/output rarity; - whether the output is random or selectable; - star-up material requirements; - duplicate-chip behavior; - dismantle/recycle/exchange rules; - daily or event limits. Until those screenshots are available, the Wiki intentionally avoids fabricating those values. Practical priority For a developing main APC: - collect recurring free Chip Materials before buying into the system; - build chips that support the primary troop faction; - check active chip setup whenever changing formation composition; - do not consume rare chips blindly if they can later support star progression or Tactical Modification unlocks. en.body: APC Parts & Parts Set Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for current Parts Set and Gears-removal changes; medium for legacy unlock levels and old material tables. en.heading: Tactical Modification
en.body: Tactical Modification Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High — unlock conditions and system purpose are explicitly documented in official patch notes. Tactical Modification is an advanced Modified Vehicle progression layer designed to convert surplus vehicle-modification resources into additional squad combat power. Unlock conditions Official October 2025 patch notes state that Tactical Modification unlocks when any one of the following conditions is met: - Vehicle transformation / Modify level reaches Lv.500 ; - all Modified Vehicle parts reach Lv.66 ; - any Orange vehicle chip reaches 10 stars . Only one route is required. This gives late-game accounts several ways to reach the system depending on where their APC investment is already strongest. Why this matters The unlock conditions connect the three mature APC branches: 1. vehicle Modify progression; 2. six-part development; 3. Orange chip star progression. A player approaching the threshold should therefore compare the marginal cost of each route rather than blindly pushing all three at once. Surplus-resource purpose The official description specifically says Tactical Modification allows survivors to use surplus vehicle modification items to enhance squads. This indicates that the system is partly a late-game sink for materials that would otherwise lose value after reaching earlier caps. Exact conversion rates, Tactical Modification levels and stat gains should be captured from the current in-game interface before being published as fixed numbers. Route-selection checklist Before choosing an unlock path: - If Modify is already near 500, finish the vehicle route. - If all six parts are clustered near 66, the all-parts route may also complete Parts Set milestones on the way. - If a core Orange chip is already highly starred, compare the cost of reaching 10★ against the other two paths. - Do not sacrifice the primary formation's immediate combat performance just to unlock the system a few days earlier. Post-unlock data to collect The next Server 504 data capture should record: - Tactical Modification level cap; - materials accepted; - conversion quantities; - stat categories gained; - whether upgrades apply globally or per squad; - event scoring interactions; - reset/refund behavior, if any. en.heading: Pet Agents — Overview
en.body: Pet Agents — Overview Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Confidence: Official for system existence, unlock building, event integration and Regulus release conditions; community-backed for detailed progression strategy. Pet Agents are a permanent growth system accessed through the Special Ops Outpost . The system was officially introduced in version 1.250.650 on 13 Jun 2026. What the system does Official patch notes confirm that Pet Agents provide: - Pet Agent Rescue; - training and growth; - broad account/stat bonuses; - powerful exclusive skills. The important design point is that Pet Agents are not a side collectible . Their growth materials are now directly tied into recurring scoring systems. Event integration Officially confirmed: - Survival Preparedness — Unit Training: consuming Pet items can score points; - Alliance Duel — Holistic Growth: consuming Pet items can score points. For Server 504 planning this means Pet materials should be treated like Hero fragments, Power Cores and other timed progression resources: do not spend automatically if a double-dip window is close. Passive-account value Community testing describes Pet Agent stats as persistent background bonuses rather than APC passengers. Examples reported by current 2026 guides include development stats such as building/research speed and combat stats such as Total Army ATK/HP. Because this detail comes from community testing rather than an official formula sheet, exact attribute pools and roll ranges remain version-sensitive. Current top-end direction The latest official Pet Agent announced in version 1.250.656 is Regulus , an S-tier Agent. Official unlock condition: 1. raise Titan to Lv.50 ; 2. complete the Regulus rescue tasks. Regulus's exclusive skill King's Decree temporarily increases Troop ATK. Server 504 operating rule When deciding whether to consume Pet resources, check three things first: 1. Is Alliance Duel Holistic Growth active or approaching? 2. Is Survival Preparedness Unit Training active or approaching? 3. Does the Pet upgrade unlock a meaningful Agent/skill breakpoint immediately? If the answer to 1 or 2 is yes and there is no urgent breakpoint, saving is usually more efficient than blind spending. en.heading: Pet Training & Growth
en.body: Pet Training & Growth Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Confidence: Official for training/growth as core systems; community-backed for attribute refinement behavior and optimization strategy. Pet growth has two different layers that should not be confused: 1. level / breakthrough progression ; 2. training / attribute refinement . Official patch notes confirm training and growth as core Pet Agent features, but do not publish the detailed formulas. Level progression Community guides describe Pet Agents as following level milestones that unlock later Agents and stronger progression tiers. A common low-spender strategy is to stop investing heavily in early low-rarity Agents after they reach the level needed for the next unlock, then preserve rarer materials for later A/S-tier Agents. This is a strategy recommendation , not an official rule. Special Training / Attribute Refinement A current 2026 community guide documents an important UI behavior: - Train rolls a new set of attributes; - the rolled attributes are not automatically committed; - Replace is required to accept the new roll. Because reroll UI is version-sensitive, the exact button wording should still be checked against Server 504's current English UI. Safe workflow 1. Note your current saved stats before training. 2. Tap Train once. 3. Compare the proposed roll. 4. If you want it, confirm it with Replace/accept before rolling again. 5. Never assume a green CP number automatically means the roll was saved. Attribute quality Community guidance emphasizes that raw CP is not always the best decision signal. Commonly valued development rolls include: - Building Speed; - Research Speed. Commonly valued late-game combat rolls include: - Total Army ATK; - Total Army HP; - faction/unit damage-type bonuses. Exact attribute pools, percentages and rarity bands are not yet canonical in this Wiki. Event timing Officially, consuming Pet items can score in: - Alliance Duel — Holistic Growth; - Survival Preparedness — Unit Training. This makes Pet leveling and training a strong candidate for double-dip planning rather than daily uncontrolled spending. Verification queue Needed from Server 504: - exact level-cap structure by Agent rarity; - breakthrough breakpoints; - exact resource per level; - all training attribute names; - roll ranges by rarity; - whether training resources themselves score, or only selected Pet-growth consumables. en.heading: Shadow Calls & Pet Rescue
en.body: Shadow Calls & Pet Rescue Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Confidence: Official for Pet Agent Rescue as a system and Regulus rescue gate; community-backed for Shadow Calls ↔ Pet resource farming behavior. Pet Agent progression includes a Rescue layer and, according to current community guides, a dispatch/economy loop through Shadow Calls . Pet Agent Rescue Official Pet Agent launch notes explicitly list Pet Agent Rescue as one of the systems unlocked through the Special Ops Outpost. The latest official Regulus patch gives a concrete example of how Rescue can gate a Pet Agent: - first reach Titan Lv.50 ; - then complete the required rescue tasks; - Regulus becomes unlockable. This suggests that Pet progression is not only a material/level grind: later Agents may also require a rescue-task stage. Shadow Calls A current community Pet guide identifies Shadow Calls dispatches as a recurring source of Pet progression materials, including experience/growth items, breakthrough-related materials and badge-type rewards. It also reports mission tags such as: - Logistics; - Combat; - Tech. Matching an Agent to the requested mission archetype is reported to improve the chance of a better dispatch result. Because exact reward tables and success-rate formulas are not official public data, they remain COMMUNITY / VERIFY SERVER 504 . Practical dispatch rule 1. Keep dispatch slots active whenever possible. 2. Match Agent tags/archetypes to mission requirements when the UI offers that distinction. 3. Prefer scarce Pet-growth resources over generic resources when reward value is otherwise comparable. 4. Do not spend rare Pet items immediately after collecting them if an Alliance Duel / Survival Preparedness double-dip window is near. Do not confuse systems Shadow Calls existed before Pet Agents and has its own broader reward mechanics. The Wiki therefore does not claim every Shadow Calls task is a Pet task. Instead, current community evidence indicates it has become one useful acquisition channel for Pet progression. en.heading: Regulus

Unlock requirement Official patch notes state: 1. raise Titan to Lv.50 ; 2. complete the associated rescue tasks ; 3. unlock Regulus. Why Regulus matters Regulus confirms several design directions for the Pet Agent system: - later S-tier Agents are gated by investment in earlier Agents; - rescue tasks remain relevant at the top end of the system; - Pet-exclusive skills can provide direct battlefield effects rather than only passive account development. A player planning for Regulus should therefore avoid evaluating Titan only by immediate CP gain. This does not mean every player should rush Titan Lv.50 regardless of event timing. Pet resources now score in Alliance Duel and Survival Preparedness, so timing the final push can create significantly better resource efficiency. en.heading: Alliance Systems — Overview
en.body: Alliance Systems — Overview Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Scope: Core alliance mechanics. Server-specific diplomacy and allocation rules belong in the Server 504 Charter / Operational Codex, not in this article. Alliances in Dark War: Survival are a progression, combat and administration layer rather than only a social group. Joining an active alliance improves account growth through Alliance Help , Alliance Tech , Alliance Gifts , coordinated rallies, reinforcements and alliance events. Core systems Alliance Help Members can assist one another to reduce construction and research timers. The personal Alliance Hall controls how much alliance-help capacity and reinforcement capacity an account can receive. Alliance Tech Alliance members donate to shared technology. Community guides consistently describe the tree as granting alliance-wide progression and combat bonuses such as construction/research efficiency and troop stats. Exact technology names, levels and numerical bonuses should be verified from current in-game UI before the Wiki publishes a full tree. Alliance Gifts Alliance activity and spending can generate shared gifts. Gift progression also acts as a gate for some alliance event functionality: official patch notes confirm that at Alliance Gifts Lv.20 , Bio-Mutant can run two Frankenstein rounds per event. Alliance administration R4/R5 ranks receive operational permissions in multiple systems. Examples documented by current sources include Armory Assault registration, Allied Power alliance-task refresh, Bio-Mutant scheduling and other event initiations. Exact permissions vary by feature. Territory and structures Alliance Centers, territory, cities, tiles and Strongholds appear across the world and seasonal conquest systems. Their attack, truce and protection rules are highly version- and season-dependent; the Wiki keeps those rules separate from permanent alliance mechanics. Game mechanic vs Server 504 policy A crucial distinction: - Game mechanic: what the game allows — registration limits, capture timers, rally/reinforcement rules, event permissions. - Server 504 policy: how alliances voluntarily coordinate those mechanics — rotations, allocations, diplomatic limits, sanctions or shared-benefit agreements. The Wiki documents the first. The Charter and Operational Codex document the second. en.heading: Alliance Help & Alliance Hall
en.body: Alliance Help & Alliance Hall Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Confidence: High for the core mechanic; exact per-level values remain community data until captured in game. Alliance Help is one of the highest-value free progression systems in Dark War: Survival. Alliance members can reduce one another's construction and research timers by tapping Help requests. Alliance Hall The personal Alliance Hall governs two important capacities: 1. Alliance Help capacity — how many helps an upgrade can receive; 2. reinforcement capacity — how many allied units can reinforce your shelter. Community Wiki data explicitly states that higher Alliance Hall levels increase reinforcement capacity and alliance-help chances. Progression importance Alliance Hall is also a recurring Watchtower prerequisite. Public progression tables show it becoming a major gate from roughly WT9 onward. Because Watchtower prerequisite tables conflict at some levels, the exact chain remains versioned in the separate Watchtower reference, but the planning rule is stable: Do not let Alliance Hall fall far behind the Watchtower. Practical use - Request Help before spending construction/research speedups. - Keep Alliance Hall progressing during long Watchtower upgrades. - In active alliances, Help compounds across dozens of upgrades and saves a significant amount of speedup inventory over time. - Reinforcement capacity matters separately from rally capacity; do not treat the two as the same stat. Verification gap The Wiki does not yet publish a complete Alliance Hall level table because public sources are incomplete and may not reflect current bonuses. A clean Server 504 capture should include: - level; - Alliance Help Cap; - reinforcement capacity; - resource cost; - build time. Sources - Fandom — Alliance Hall: - Pocket Gamer — Alliance Help overview: - BlueStacks — Alliance Guide:

en.heading: Alliance Tech
en.body: Alliance Tech Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Confidence: High for system purpose; exact tree and numerical bonuses still require current in-game capture. Alliance Tech is a shared progression tree funded by member donations. Unlike personal Research Center technology, Alliance Tech benefits the alliance collectively. What it does Current community guides consistently describe Alliance Tech as covering two broad categories: - development bonuses — construction/research efficiency and related account-growth effects; - combat bonuses — troop attack/defense and other military improvements. Because the exact technology names, maximum levels and bonus values can change, the Wiki does not yet publish a full numeric tree. Contribution loop The stable player routine is: 1. open Alliance Tech; 2. donate to the alliance's current priority technology; 3. receive the associated alliance contribution/currency where applicable; 4. let alliance leadership coordinate focus so donations are not scattered across low-priority branches. Why focused donations matter Alliance Tech is a shared resource pool. Ten members donating into ten unrelated branches can produce less immediate value than the same donations completing one high-impact technology first. This is a game-system observation , not a Server 504 governance rule. Which technology should be prioritized at any given time belongs to alliance leadership and can change with season, event and roster needs. Data still needed To make this page a proper database, capture current UI for: - technology category; - technology name; - level / max level; - donation requirement; - alliance resource requirement if shown; - effect per level; - prerequisite technology. en.heading: Alliance Gifts
en.body: Alliance Gifts Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Confidence: High for the system's existence and the Lv.20 Bio-Mutant gate; exact gift XP/reward tables are not yet canonical. Alliance Gifts are shared alliance rewards generated through alliance activity and purchases. They are one of the reasons active alliances accelerate account growth even for members who are not the ones spending. What Alliance Gifts provide Community sources consistently describe Alliance Gifts as a source of free rewards such as resources, speedups and premium-value items. Exact gift contents depend on gift type and current game version. Alliance Gifts level Alliance Gifts also have a progression level. This is not merely cosmetic: official patch notes confirm a direct gameplay gate at Alliance Gifts Lv.20 . At Lv.20 or higher, an alliance can activate two Frankenstein rounds during one Bio-Mutant event. Official conditions include: - round 2 must start at least 10 minutes after round 1 ends; - each survivor may participate in only one round per event; - each survivor receives rewards only once; - registering for both rounds delays reward distribution until the second round concludes. Operational implication Alliance Gifts level therefore affects alliance event flexibility. A higher-level alliance can split members across separate Frankenstein windows, which helps alliances spanning multiple time zones. Data still needed The Wiki does not yet publish a complete Gift Level table. Current in-game captures should record: - Gift Level; - XP required to next level; - reward changes by level if any; - gift categories and contents; - expiration/claim rules if shown. en.heading: Armory Assault
en.body: Armory Assault Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Confidence: Community-verified event rules. Server 504 allocation practice is intentionally excluded from this game-mechanics article. Armory Assault is an alliance-vs-alliance event centered on controlling one of 8 Armories . Registration Current community reference states: - alliance leader or R4 can register; - an alliance can register for up to 2 Armories ; - registration uses multiple time-slot selections; - if multiple alliances contest the same Armory, scheduling is determined from overlapping selected time slots; - holding an Armory in the previous round can trigger automatic registration for that same Armory in the next round; - the event operates in a 4-round cycle , after which Armory occupation is reset. Because these rules are community-sourced rather than current official patch text, Server 504 should verify the registration screen whenever the cycle structure changes. Battle rules Community data describes the battle as follows: - alliances attack an Armory through rallies; - defenders reinforce it; - a battle can last up to 2 hours ; - holding continuous control for 30 minutes captures the Armory for the round; - if no alliance completes a 30-minute continuous hold, the alliance controlling it when the battle ends wins the round. Participation restriction Players who join the alliance only after registration closes may be ineligible for that Armory battle. This makes roster timing important before registration lock. Rewards Each of the 8 Armories can provide a different reward category. Community documentation lists examples such as: - speedups; - Orange Hero Fragments; - equipment-related materials; - Boost Ores. A critical distinction is that reward assignments can rotate . The physical Armory identity and its current reward should therefore be treated as separate fields in any Server 504 tracking table. Game mechanic vs Server 504 allocation The game provides registration, battle and reward mechanics. Any voluntary agreement about which Server 504 alliance uses which Armory is a server operational policy , not a universal Armory Assault rule. Verification queue Useful current screenshots: - registration limit and cycle count; - exact five time slots; - current 8 Armory reward table; - capture/hold timer text; - participation lock wording. Sources - DarkWarData — Armory Assault Event:

en.heading: Capital & Turrets
en.body: Capital & Turrets Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Confidence: High for the current rally/reinforcement rules because they are confirmed in official patch notes. Capital and Turrets are major state-level combat objectives used in Capital Clash and State of Supremacy contexts. Current rally and reinforcement model Official December 2025 patch notes changed the old single-rally/single-reinforcement behavior: - rally limits for Capital and Turrets were removed; - survivors can launch multiple rallies to the same objective; - survivors can send multiple reinforcement squads ; - when launching a rally or reinforcement to a Capital/Turret, troop capacity receives an additional +40,000 . This is a current mechanic and should override older guides that describe one rally queue per objective. Strategic consequence The objective is no longer simply “fill one rally and one garrison.” Modern fights can involve parallel rally cycles and multiple reinforcement streams. This increases the importance of: - rally-lead selection; - reinforcement timing; - formation/faction coordination; - hospital capacity and healing planning; - keeping secondary marches available instead of committing every march at once. Capital Clash schedule visibility Official February 2026 notes added a phase schedule directly to the Capital Clash event page, helping alliances coordinate preparation and battle windows from the game UI. State Hospital connection For State of Supremacy, official notes warn that untreated units remaining in the State Hospital are permanently lost when the hospital closes at Tuesday 00:00 server time after the event. Presidency and governance Capturing or controlling the Capital can connect to state presidency and official-position systems, but the game mechanic does not prescribe a Server 504 political rotation. Any rotation or shared-governance arrangement is a separate server policy. Sources - Apple App Store — official version history, Capital Clash / State of Supremacy rally and reinforcement changes:

en.heading: Alliance Centers, Territory & Strongholds
en.body: Alliance Centers, Territory & Strongholds Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Confidence: High for official 2026 season-specific changes; universal territory rules remain versioned because conquest mechanics differ by season. Alliance structures and territory systems become increasingly important in later seasonal conquest. The key caution is that territory rules are not static across every season . Alliance Centers Alliance Centers are attackable alliance structures used in territory and war systems. Official February 2026 patch notes explicitly reference alliance centers as structures whose durability can be demolished with repeated attacks. Community Glory War documentation describes an ordered attack path for enemy Alliance Centers: Alliance Center I → Alliance Center II → Alliance Center III and reports that Alliance Centers can contribute event-specific Glory Point bonuses. Because those values belong to Glory War, they should not be generalized to every season. Territory / tiles Territory connects alliance or camp-controlled structures. Current official conquest patches show that tile rules can include: - protected and attackable windows; - connectable targets such as allied tiles, camp cities and oases; - garrisoning; - reinforcement caps; - short post-capture protection/truce periods; - durability and on-fire mechanics. These values have been actively rebalanced, so the Wiki should always attach a season/version label to exact tile numbers. Strongholds Strongholds are major territorial control points in conquest seasons. Official April 2026 changes include: - Strongholds and tiles inside their area can be protected outside designated War Declaration periods; - capturing an enemy-camp Stronghold or a neutral Stronghold inside enemy territory can trigger a 1-hour truce ; - Origin Lands Strongholds were repositioned; - after capture, members of the owner's camp can teleport shelters inside the Stronghold region; - enemy-camp members cannot teleport into that controlled Stronghold region; - Stronghold protection was standardized to 60 minutes in the cited Origin Lands update. These are Origin Lands / conquest-season rules , not permanent global rules. City capture and truce The same April 2026 official notes adjusted Territory Triumph: - War Declaration duration was reduced from 4 hours to 2.5 hours ; - capturing a Neutral / Enemy Camp city triggers a 1.5-hour truce ; - other captures use a much shorter truce window. Again, this is versioned conquest content. Cross-state protection example Historical Mutant Mines community notes also show that territory/Watchtower attack permissions can change by zone: cross-state players may be prevented from attacking Watchtowers outside Lost Lands while those protections are removed in the Capital area. That historical event rule is retained only as an investigation example until reconfirmed in current Server 504 UI. This is why the Wiki stores season , event , zone and version alongside any territory rule. Sources - Apple App Store — official 2026 Territory Triumph / Stronghold / Origin Lands changes: - DarkWarData — Glory War:

en.heading: Shops & Currencies Overview
en.body: Shops & Currencies Overview Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Scope: Free exchange shops, season/event shops and current-vs-legacy currency naming. Rule: Shop inventory and purchase limits are version-sensitive. Server 504 in-game UI overrides public guides. Dark War: Survival has several exchange systems that use different currencies and reset schedules. The most important change for reading older guides is that Capital Shop, Black Gold Shop and Arena Shop are being consolidated into a unified Honor Shop . Current shop map Shop / exchange Main purpose Currency Status --- --- --- --- Honor Shop Rare combat/equipment materials Honor Points Officially introduced; rollout was staged Alliance Shop Research, hero fragments, safety and utility items Personal Points / Alliance currency Current community-verified Season Shop Season-limited progression, skins and upgrade materials Season-specific currency/points Rotates by season VIP Shop VIP-gated recurring materials and utility items Verify current UI Current; stock varies by VIP/state Combat Shop Combat-earned exchange items, including equipment references Mode-specific currency Still referenced in recent 2026 guides Trial Shop Trial-mode rewards / lucky equipment references Mode-specific currency Still referenced in recent 2026 guides Trade Shop / Merchant Guild Trading and Merchant Guild systems Feature-specific Officially expanded in 2026 Event exchange shops Temporary event rewards Event-specific currency Temporary; do not carry rules across events The major 2026 shop migration Official update notes announced: - Capital Shop + Black Gold Shop + Arena Shop → Honor Shop ; - currencies from State of Supremacy, Capital Clash and Black Gold Battlefield → Honor Points ; - 1 Capital Glory Badge → 40 Honor Points ; - 1 Black Gold Coin → 2 Honor Points . The rollout was initially announced for selected early States. Therefore, an older source saying “buy this from Capital Shop” may still describe the correct acquisition family but use a legacy shop name. How this Wiki handles old shop references When an item database says: - Capital Shop , - Black Gold Shop , or - Arena Shop , this Wiki treats the source as legacy naming and checks whether the item now belongs to the Honor Shop in the current Server 504 UI. The old source is not deleted because it still helps identify where the item historically entered the economy. Purchase-priority rule Shop priority should follow the account bottleneck, not a permanent tier list. A useful default order is: 1. scarce permanent progression material; 2. main-formation star/equipment breakpoint; 3. Industrial/APC bottleneck; 4. war utility that prevents losses shield/teleport ; 5. event-timed speedups; 6. farmable resources last. Late-game accounts may reverse some priorities once a research tree or equipment tier is complete. Version warning Do not copy exact prices, weekly limits or stock tables into a permanent guide without a current screenshot. The developer has repeatedly merged shops, changed packs and altered event currencies. Sources - Official-version-history mirror — Honor Shop merger and Honor Point conversion: - Apple App Store — current Dark War: Survival version history: - LDShop — Alliance Shop guide, Jul 2026: - LDShop — equipment/shop references, Jul 2026:

en.heading: Honor Shop
en.body: Honor Shop Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Confidence: High for the official merger/conversion rules; medium for exact current Server 504 stock. Server 504 status: Verify the live UI because rollout was staged by State. The Honor Shop is the unified exchange system introduced to replace several older PvP/event shops. Official migration Official update notes state that these shops are merged into the Honor Shop : - Capital Shop; - Black Gold Shop; - Arena Shop. The same update replaces currencies earned from: - State of Supremacy; - Capital Clash; - Black Gold Battlefield with Honor Points . Currency conversion The official conversion announced was: - 1 Capital Glory Badge = 40 Honor Points ; - 1 Black Gold Coin = 2 Honor Points . Why older guides look different Many 2025 item pages still list Power Cores, Boost Ores, Orange Versatile Hero Fragments, Titanium Alloy or Design Blueprints under Capital/Arena/Black Gold shops. en.heading: Alliance Shop
en.body: Alliance Shop Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Confidence: High for current 2026 community inventory categories; exact prices/limits remain UI-dependent. The Alliance Shop is one of the most dependable free recurring exchange systems because its currency is tied to alliance activity rather than one short event. Currency Recent 2026 community documentation calls the shop currency Personal Points . Players also commonly refer to the silver currency as Alliance Coins/Alliance Points. Common ways to earn Personal Points include: - Alliance Tech donations; - Alliance Help activity; - alliance events such as Zombie Siege; - regular alliance participation. Current high-value stock categories Recent 2026 sources list: - Wisdom Medals; - Orange Versatile Hero Fragments; - Advanced Teleporters; - Peace Shields; - construction/research/training/general speedups; - resource packs and Coins; - selected lower-rarity hero fragments. Default purchase priorities 1. Wisdom Medals After Duel/Battle Strategy research is unlocked and still incomplete, Wisdom Medals are usually one of the highest-value weekly purchases because they gate advanced research. 2. Orange Versatile Hero Fragments These remain valuable because they advance Orange/S-rarity hero stars and therefore skill progression. Concentrating fragments into a long-term core hero is generally more efficient than spreading them across many heroes. 3. Advanced Teleporters and Peace Shields These are not CP materials but can prevent much larger losses during war periods. Maintain a tactical reserve rather than treating them as emergency Ruby purchases. 4. Speedups Useful when matched with Alliance Duel / Survival Preparedness / other scoring windows. 5. Basic resources Usually last priority because they have more farmable sources. Important legacy warning Recent 2026 Alliance Shop guides specifically warn that Capital Teleporters are no longer available there ; Advanced Teleporters cover the relevant modern relocation use. Old shop checklists that still tell players to buy Capital Teleporters should be treated as outdated. Event-timing principle Buying an item and using an item are separate decisions. Examples: - buy Wisdom Medals during the weekly reset, but spend them when research/event timing is favorable; - buy Orange Versatile Fragments, then consume them during hero-star scoring if practical; - store speedups for the matching construction/research/training objective. Safety items are the exception: use shields/teleports immediately when needed. en.heading: Season Shop & VIP Shop
en.body: Season Shop & VIP Shop Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Confidence: Medium-high for recurring item categories; exact stock, currency cost and limits are version/season/VIP dependent. Season Shop and VIP Shop are recurring sources for scarce progression materials, but neither should be documented with a permanent price table unless Server 504 provides a current screenshot. Season Shop Historical and recent community references associate the Season Shop with materials such as: - Power Cores; - Boost Ores; - Orange Versatile Hero Fragments; - Orange equipment / equipment boxes; - Titanium Alloy; - Design Blueprints; - season-specific permanent skins or account-wide bonuses. Recent 2026 strategy guides increasingly recommend comparing temporary materials against permanent season rewards such as building/shelter skins or other account-wide bonuses before spending season currency. Season Shop rule The best purchase is not always the rarest-looking item. Ask: 1. Is the item a current hard bottleneck? 2. Can it be farmed elsewhere every week? 3. Is there a permanent season-limited reward that disappears when the season ends? 4. Does buying now unlock a meaningful breakpoint before the shop closes? Exact inventory changes between seasons and server progression stages. VIP Shop Legacy item databases list the VIP Shop as a source for: - Power Cores; - Boost Ores; - Orange Versatile Hero Fragments. Recent 2026 community guides also reference Golden Wrenches and Coins/Gold as useful VIP Shop purchases depending on account stage and event timing. The shop's actual stock and value depend on VIP level and current patch, so the Wiki does not publish a universal VIP-level price table without in-game evidence. Timing with events Materials that score in recurring events should usually be purchased when available but consumed when useful . Examples: - Golden Wrenches: hold for vehicle/APC-related scoring windows when possible; - Power Cores: use when the main formation is ready and/or when the event schedule rewards the spend; - Hero fragments: align star-up spending with relevant scoring windows when practical. Do not delay an upgrade that materially affects an immediate server war simply for marginal event points. Paid packs are a separate economy The Pack Shop / Special Offers are not the same thing as free exchange shops. Official 2026 patch notes continue to add/remove pack tabs and change purchase limits, including a Mod Vehicle Chip Pack and increased Precision Parts Pack limit. Because paid inventory changes quickly, this Wiki records only stable system relationships, not pack-value rankings. en.heading: Equipment & APC Material Sources
en.body: Equipment & APC Material Sources Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Scope: Hero-equipment and Modified Vehicle/APC materials only. Rule: Separate materials by system so similarly named items are not mixed. Dark War: Survival has several high-value materials that look similar in inventory but belong to completely different progression systems. Hero equipment track Boost Ores Used to enhance hero equipment through the normal enhancement track. Legacy community sources list: - Armory Assault; - Bio-Mutant; - seasonal Equipment Battle Pass; - VIP Shop; - Season Shop; - Trial Shop; - legacy Capital / Black Gold shop sources; - selected offers. Because Boost Ores have several repeatable sources, they are usually less strategically scarce than Power Cores or DX Blueprints. Power Cores Used after Orange equipment reaches the relevant enhancement gate. Public item data describes Orange equipment becoming eligible for Power Core upgrades after enhancement Lv.20. Source families include: - Season Shop; - VIP Shop; - Honor-family / legacy Capital-Arena-Black Gold sources; - Trial Shop; - Total War / other milestone events; - Bio-Mutant individual rewards; - offers. DX Blueprints DX Blueprints belong to late hero-equipment / red-equipment breakthrough , not the APC. Recent 2026 community guides report them in the Honor Shop and other high-end reward routes. Exact prices/weekly limits should be confirmed in Server 504. APC / Modified Vehicle track Titanium Alloy Used to enhance APC parts. Documented source families include: - Capital Clash participation/ranking rewards; - Zombie Siege; - Season Shop; - legacy Black Gold / Honor-family shop sources; - selected offers. Design Blueprint Used for advanced APC part progression after the early part levels. Legacy item data lists: - Season Shop; - Black Gold Shop now a legacy Honor-family reference where the merger is active ; - selected offers. Design Blueprint and DX Blueprint are different items. Vehicle Parts / Gears / chip materials The Modified Vehicle system has been changed by later patches, including Parts Sets, chips and Tactical Modification. Older APC material charts can therefore become structurally outdated even when the material name is still correct. Use the current APC article for the modern system architecture and treat older exact recipes as verification targets. Quick decision table Material System Spend when... Avoid when... --- --- --- --- Boost Ores Hero equipment Main formation has equipment worth enhancing You are dumping them into disposable lower-tier gear Power Cores Orange hero equipment Orange gear has reached the Power Core gate and the formation is long-term The gear/hero is temporary or event timing is poor DX Blueprint Red hero equipment A real red breakthrough is reachable You are months away from the prerequisite gear state Titanium Alloy APC parts The chosen APC part path is defined You are upgrading randomly because the button is available Design Blueprint APC parts Later APC recipe explicitly requires it You confused it with DX Blueprint Source-history warning Several 2025 item pages name Capital Shop, Arena Shop and Black Gold Shop independently.
