en.heading: Event & Premium Currencies
en.body: Event & Premium Currencies Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Scope: Temporary exchange currencies and paid virtual currency. Rule: Event currencies can disappear with the event; spend/expiry rules must be verified in the current event UI. Dark War: Survival regularly introduces temporary currencies for seasonal and limited-time events. These should not be stored in the Wiki as if they were permanent account currencies. Honor Points Status: Official current-system currency. Official update notes state that currencies from State of Supremacy, Capital Clash and Black Gold Battlefield are replaced by Honor Points as the unified Honor Shop system rolls out. Legacy conversion rules announced by the developer: - 1 Capital Glory Badge → 40 Honor Points; - 1 Black Gold Coin → 2 Honor Points. Personal Points / Alliance currency Status: Current community-verified. Used in the Alliance Shop. Recent 2026 guides list Alliance Tech donations, Alliance Help and alliance event activity as repeatable sources. Community language sometimes calls these Alliance Coins/Alliance Points; the Wiki prefers the current UI wording when a Server 504 screenshot is available. Mechanical Components Status: Community-documented event currency. Industrial Surge uses Mechanical Components as an exchange material. Community data describes obtaining them from Radar events and Steel Zombies, then exchanging them for Precision Parts and other Industrial materials. Magatama Status: Sealed Island / Blood Moon community reference — verify Server 504 UI. Community Sealed Island guides describe Magatama as a limited Blood Moon exchange currency obtained from Blood Moon enemies such as Rotting Oni / Booze Brute variants and spent in a temporary exchange shop. Public guides disagree on season numbering and can differ on shop naming, costs, weekly limits and whether unused Magatama expires. Server 504's current event UI is authoritative for all of those fields. Do not publish a permanent Magatama cost table until captured in-game. Shell Coins Status: Official limited-time event currency. The Jul 2026 official App Store notes introduced the Summer Snap event and explicitly state that participation awards Shell Coins , exchangeable for rare items, exclusive skins and other rewards. This is a good example of why event currencies belong in a versioned index rather than the permanent economy model. Dawn Badges Status: Official paid virtual currency. The official Dark War payment center defines Dawn Badges as an in-game virtual item used to exchange for: - packs; - weekly passes; - monthly passes; - battle passes. Important official rule: purchasing Dawn Badges on the website does not itself grant VIP Points . VIP Points are credited when Dawn Badges are exchanged for qualifying packs in-game. Dawn Badges cannot be transferred between UIDs. Rubies / premium in-game currency Rubies remain a broad in-game premium currency used across convenience, attempts, refreshes and other purchases. Exact recommended Ruby spending changes with progression and event schedule, so the Wiki does not maintain a single permanent “best Ruby use” table. en.heading: Events Overview
en.body: Events Overview Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for event names/current existence; medium for exact scoring because event rules are adjusted by patches. Dark War: Survival progression is strongly event-driven. Many resources that can be spent at any time are more valuable when used during the matching event window. Alliance Duel Alliance Duel is a recurring alliance competition built around themed scoring days. Common scoring categories include building, research, hero development, troop development and broader growth activities. Recent official updates show that the scoring model continues to evolve. For example, Pet item consumption was added to the Holistic Growth theme in 2026. Practical rule Do not assume an old Alliance Duel point table is permanent. Save major upgrade resources when possible, then verify the current event interface before spending. Survival Preparedness Survival Preparedness is another recurring progression event with theme-based tasks and ranking rewards. Official 2026 patch notes added Pet item consumption to the Unit Training theme and also changed matchmaking so opponents can be drawn from the player's Alliance Duel League group with similar Watchtower levels. State of Supremacy / Capital conflict State of Supremacy includes cross-state competition and capital warfare. Community event data describes capital control time as an important victory condition, with state leadership / president appointment tied to the result. Exact scoring values and escort-point rules have been patched multiple times, so publish mechanics separately from point tables. Zombie Siege Zombie Siege is an alliance-defense event where members prepare formations and reinforce shelters against waves. Official patches have expanded the maximum difficulty and improved defense controls. Bio-Mutant Bio-Mutant is an alliance damage event. Community data identifies it as a recurring source of valuable materials such as Power Cores at higher damage milestones. Event placement and timing rules can change, so verify the current event panel. Other recurring and special events The game also rotates many additional systems, including examples such as: - Shadow Calls - Dark Syndicate escort content - Arena and Champion Duel - Peak of Glory - Black Gold Battlefield - Fishing and seasonal mini-events - Mutant Mines and season-specific PvP modes - temporary celebration events Server 504 event-writing standard Each event article should answer five questions: 1. What is the objective? 2. When does it happen? Use server time. 3. What should players save beforehand? 4. What actions score or matter? 5. What should alliance leadership coordinate? Exact scoring charts should always carry a verification date. en.heading: Alliance Duel
en.body: Alliance Duel Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for the weekly structure and current official changes; medium for exact scoring values because the task table has changed over time. Alliance Duel is a week-long alliance-vs-alliance competition. Each day uses a different scoring theme, so the event rewards planning more than uncontrolled daily spending. Core structure Community event data consistently describes the event as a daily-theme competition between two alliances. Each day awards points for specific actions such as construction, research, hero development, troop development, APC growth or PvP. The alliance with the higher daily score wins that day, while the overall duel is settled across the week. Current official patch notes also confirm that in the Conquest/State Duel context, Day 6 is Enemy Buster Day . Why resource timing matters Many Alliance Duel actions consume materials that are also useful elsewhere. Common examples include: - construction and research speedups; - Wisdom Medals; - hero fragments; - Exclusive Equipment fragments; - Power Cores; - Hero Equipment Lucky Chests; - Precision Parts; - APC / Modified Vehicle materials; - troop training and promotion resources; - selected Pet Agent items. A strong account does not necessarily score by spending more; it scores by spending at the correct time. Current version-sensitive changes Official 2026 patch notes added a new mission to the Holistic Growth theme that awards points for consuming Pet items. Official season notes also confirm that Alliance Duel Day 6 can become Enemy Buster Day during Conquest/State Duel content. Because scoring tables evolve, an old point chart should be treated as a historical reference only. Enemy Buster Enemy Buster is the PvP-focused day. Practical preparation usually includes: - Advanced Teleporters; - shields for players who are not participating in combat; - hospital capacity and healing resources; - clearly assigned rally and reinforcement roles; - target discipline to avoid wasting troops; - awareness of cross-state teleport rules. Official 2026 changes allow direct cross-state relocation by selecting a location on the opponent State map during supported cross-state events such as Alliance Duel Enemy Buster. Duel research and long-term value Community strategy discussion consistently treats Duel research as a high-value long-term investment because it improves Alliance Duel efficiency and rewards. Exact tech effects should be verified in the current Research Center before publishing a fixed table. What to save A practical rolling reserve is: Category Typical materials to reserve --- --- Construction speedups, Precision Parts, structure resources Research speedups, Wisdom Medals Heroes recruitment tickets, hero fragments, Exclusive Equipment fragments Equipment Power Cores, Hero Equipment Lucky Chests APC Titanium Alloy, Design Blueprints, chips / chip materials Troops training speedups, promotion-ready units PvP teleporters, healing capacity, shields The current event interface always has priority over this table. Alliance coordination Leadership should publish a short weekly plan covering: 1. which days the alliance intends to push hard; 2. which scarce materials members should hold; 3. minimum target milestones if the alliance uses them; 4. Enemy Buster participation and shield policy; 5. whether seasonal or server events overlap the same resources. The Game Wiki should explain the event mechanics. en.heading: Survival Preparedness
en.body: Survival Preparedness Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for current matchmaking and Pet-item changes; medium for exact task-point tables because scoring can be patched. Survival Preparedness is a recurring progression event built around rotating task themes. It overlaps heavily with Alliance Duel, which makes resource timing especially important. Event model Community event data describes Survival Preparedness as a multi-day event with time-windowed themes such as: - Shelter Expansion; - Hero Trial; - Unit Training; - Elimination Program; - Modification Contest; - Equipment-focused growth; - mixed Arms Expert-style tasks. Different themes reward different upgrade materials and activities, so the strongest strategy is usually to prepare resources before the matching window opens. Current matchmaking Official December 2025 patch notes changed matchmaking: - previously, opponents were selected from the player's current State with similar Watchtower levels; - now, opponents are selected from the player's Alliance Duel League group , while still considering similar Watchtower levels; - ranking rewards were increased at the same time. This means Survival Preparedness should not be treated as purely an internal-State leaderboard anymore. Pet Agent integration Official June 2026 patch notes added a new mission to the Unit Training theme: consuming Pet items can now earn points. This is a good example of why fixed 2025 scoring charts cannot be copied unchanged into the current Wiki. Common resource overlap Survival Preparedness often overlaps with resources also used in Alliance Duel: Progression area Typical resources --- --- Buildings construction speedups, Precision Parts Research research speedups, Wisdom Medals Heroes Prime Recruitment, hero fragments Training troop training / promotion speedups Equipment Power Cores, equipment chests APC Titanium Alloy, Design Blueprints PvE Radar events, Roaming Zombies, Boomer rallies Pets selected Pet Agent training/growth items The exact active task list shown in-game is the authoritative source for that event cycle. Double-dip principle The key optimization concept is double dipping : perform an upgrade when it scores in more than one active event at the same time. Examples can include: - construction during a matching Survival Preparedness window and Alliance Duel construction theme; - hero fragments during overlapping hero-growth windows; - troop promotion when both events reward training; - equipment or APC resources when matching themes overlap. The actual overlap schedule is server- and cycle-dependent, so the Wiki should teach the principle rather than publish a permanent clock table. What to save Useful reserves include: - Precision Parts; - Wisdom Medals; - hero fragments; - Power Cores; - Hero Equipment Lucky Chests; - Titanium Alloy and Design Blueprints; - troop training speedups; - construction/research speedups; - Pet Agent resources after checking current task eligibility. Practical workflow 1. Check the upcoming theme before reset. 2. Compare it against the current Alliance Duel day. 3. Hold resources that can score twice. 4. Use PvE tasks such as zombies, Boomers or Radar when a material-spending theme is not efficient. 5. Avoid spending a scarce item simply because it scores if doing so damages long-term progression. en.heading: State of Supremacy
en.body: State of Supremacy Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for current official cross-state, Capital/Turret and State Hospital rules; medium for older preparation-phase scoring tables. State of Supremacy is a cross-state competition that combines preparation scoring with large-scale PvP and Capital control. High-level phases Community event references describe three broad phases: 1. Preparation — multi-day progression scoring similar to Alliance Duel. 2. War — cross-state PvP and Capital/Turret fighting. 3. Recovery / State Hospital settlement — treatment and revival-related mechanics after the main battle. The exact event interface should be checked each cycle because the developers continue to adjust cross-state rules. Cross-state movement Official March 2026 changes improved cross-state teleporting: - during supported cross-state events, including State of Supremacy, players can select a relocation position directly on the opponent State map; - Advanced Teleporters can be used for relocation in the Lost Lands Capital area; - same-State survivors are visually differentiated during cross-state activity. Official notes also state that during State of Supremacy, players cannot attack troops belonging to other survivors from their own State. This reduces accidental friendly fire. Capital and Turret combat Official December 2025 changes removed the old single-rally/single-reinforcement limits for the Capital and Turrets. Players can now: - launch multiple rallies against these objectives; - send multiple reinforcement squads; - receive an additional 40,000 troop capacity when launching a rally or reinforcing a Capital/Turret target. Because this materially changes command structure, older guides describing a one-target-at-a-time restriction are outdated. Winning the Capital fight Older community references describe Capital occupation time as a major victory condition. For practical coordination, leadership should treat the event as an objective-control battle rather than a simple kill-point contest. Key operational questions are: - which alliance or rally leads hold the Capital; - which teams pressure Turrets; - who reinforces versus who rallies; - how hospitals and recovery capacity are managed; - when to rotate damaged formations; - how to avoid unnecessary shelter-burning losses outside the main objectives. State Hospital Official December 2025 patch notes warn that after State of Supremacy ends, untreated units in the State Hospital must be handled before the hospital closes at server time Tuesday 00:00 . Units left untreated after closure can be permanently lost. This deadline is important enough to include in the Wiki, but players should still confirm the current event UI in case the developer changes the schedule. Experimental loss-reduction rule A December 2025 update introduced an Experimental Feature on days when State of Supremacy, Alliance Duel Enemy Buster and Capital Clash begin. During the beta, unit losses from attacking shelters were reduced by 50%. Because the feature was explicitly described as experimental and initially rolled out gradually, it should not be assumed active on every State without checking the current buff/event notice. Preparation checklist Before War Phase, prepare: - Advanced Teleporters; - healing speedups/resources and hospital capacity; - multiple combat-ready formations; - rally/reinforcement presets; - shields for noncombatants; - clear State-level target and Capital/Turret assignments; - communication channels for rapid rally changes. Wiki vs. server operations This article documents the game mechanics. Server 504-specific diplomacy, NAP decisions, command roles, Capital allocation or cross-alliance military orders belong in the Operational Codex or live Council notice. en.heading: Zombie Siege
en.body: Zombie Siege Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for current duration/interval and scoring-rule changes; medium for optimal reinforcement tactics because alliance strength differs. Zombie Siege is an alliance-defense event in which waves of zombies attack member shelters. Personal and alliance performance depend on surviving waves and using reinforcements efficiently. Core rules Community event data describes the main structure as follows: - R4/R5 can start the event; - zombies attack alliance members in waves; - a member stops receiving attacks after the shelter is breached twice; - successful defenses generate Defense Points; - reinforcing allies can also generate points; - personal and alliance ranking rewards are settled after the event. Current pacing Official August 2025 patch notes significantly shortened the event: - duration changed from 62.5 minutes to 37.5 minutes ; - zombie attack interval changed from 150 seconds to 90 seconds ; - zombie attack power increased while zombie HP decreased, with overall strength intended to remain similar; - zombies now attack from the territory closest to the alliance assembly point. Any old guide built around the 62.5-minute pacing is therefore outdated. Current Defense Point rule Official December 2025 notes changed an important scoring detail. Previously, a shelter with no garrisoned troops could fail to receive Defense Points even if the defense succeeded. Under the newer rule, the shelter owner earns Defense Points as long as the shelter successfully defends. Reinforcing squads continue to earn points according to their kill contribution. Practical defense model A safe baseline strategy is: 1. keep the strongest main formation protecting your own shelter as waves become dangerous; 2. use spare marches to reinforce members who can still survive later waves; 3. monitor wounded troops and hospital load between waves; 4. recall damaged reinforcements when needed, heal, then redeploy; 5. after your own shelter has been eliminated from further waves, reinforce surviving stronger shelters to continue contributing. Community discussion commonly recommends keeping your strongest march at home in difficult phases while using secondary marches for reinforcement points. Reinforcement priorities Do not reinforce randomly. Useful priorities are: - members whose shelters are still active in the event; - high-survivability members likely to survive deeper waves; - alliance-defined gate/tower/critical positions where applicable; - targets with space for useful troops rather than already-full low-efficiency garrisons. Before the event Alliance leadership should: - announce the event start time; - ensure members are online where possible; - remind members to heal before start; - define whether spare marches should reinforce weaker or stronger members first; - identify high-survivability shelters for late-wave reinforcement; - ensure new players understand that fighting zombies outside the shelter is not the same as defending Siege waves. Rewards and material value Community item data lists Titanium Alloy among materials obtainable from Zombie Siege, making the event relevant to APC progression as well as alliance rankings. Reward tables can change, so the current event reward panel should be treated as authoritative. en.heading: Bio-Mutant — Frankenstein
en.body: Bio-Mutant — Frankenstein Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for current round rules and timing changes; medium for damage thresholds/reward tables because alliance tiers and patches can change them. Bio-Mutant , commonly referred to as the Frankenstein event, is an alliance damage event. R4/R5 leadership schedules or starts the target, alliance members rally it, and rewards are based on personal and alliance damage. Core event flow Community event data describes the event as: 1. R4/R5 starts or schedules Frankenstein. 2. The target appears near the summoner's shelter. 3. Alliance members rally the target during the active window. 4. Attacks do not consume normal energy for the event target. 5. Rewards are settled from personal damage and total alliance damage. The exact reward thresholds shown in old charts should not be treated as permanent. Two-round system Official January 2026 patch notes added a major rule for developed alliances: - once Alliance Gifts reach Lv.20 , two Frankenstein rounds can be activated in one Bio-Mutant event; - round 2 must begin at least 10 minutes after round 1 ends ; - each survivor may participate in only one round per event ; - each survivor can receive rewards only once per event; - if a survivor registers for both rounds, reward settlement occurs after round 2 concludes. This creates a leadership decision: split members across two rounds to maximize participation and total alliance output instead of stacking every strong player into the same round. Placement interval Official January 2026 notes also clarified that, except for the initial placement, there is a 10-minute interval between Frankenstein placements. Damage optimization Community event guidance consistently recommends: - join the strongest efficient rally available; - use the highest-tier troops your account can sustain; - align hero faction, troop faction and APC/chip setup; - ensure the rally leader has strong rally capacity and combat stats; - avoid wasting a limited participation opportunity on a poor preset; - verify the formation before the event begins rather than rebuilding during the active window. Leadership coordination For one-round events, leadership should prioritize a start time with the highest possible attendance. For two-round events, leadership should decide before the first summon: - which players are assigned to Round 1; - which players are assigned to Round 2; - whether major rally leads should be divided between rounds; - how to handle members who can attend only one time slot; - when each Frankenstein will be placed. Because each survivor only receives one participation/reward opportunity, the two-round feature is primarily an attendance and alliance-damage optimization tool. Rewards Community data identifies Bio-Mutant as a source of valuable growth materials, including Power Cores at sufficiently high personal damage milestones and equipment-enhancement materials such as Boost Ores . Exact damage thresholds and reward quantities are version-sensitive and should be captured from the current Server 504 event interface before being published as a numeric table. What to prepare Before the event: - heal troops; - load the correct combat preset; - check hero equipment and Exclusive Equipment; - check APC/chips; - avoid sending your strongest march away on a long task near start time; - confirm which round you are assigned to if the alliance uses two rounds. en.heading: Season 4 — Sealed Island
en.body: Season 4 — Sealed Island Server 504 naming: Season 4 · Sealed Island Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for Server 504 season naming and officially patched Sealed Island systems; medium for community-only side-event details. Sealed Island is the current seasonal framework used by Server 504. It combines temporary progression buildings, Virus Resistance , Miasma , Oni-themed enemies, Blood Moon phases and alliance-wide seasonal activities. Quick reference - Season Buildings — Oni Seal Hall & Quartz Factory /wiki/sealed-island-season-buildings - Miasma & Virus Resistance /wiki/miasma-and-virus-resistance - Blood Moon Shroud /wiki/blood-moon-shroud - Rotting Oni & Booze Brute /wiki/rotting-oni-and-booze-brute - Oni King /wiki/oni-king - Sacred Tree Blessing /wiki/sacred-tree-blessing - Float Parade /wiki/float-parade Core progression loop A useful simplified model is: 1. obtain seasonal building resources; 2. develop Quartz Factories ; 3. use Quartz/season resources to upgrade the Oni Seal Hall ; 4. raise Virus Resistance ; 5. defeat stronger infected enemies and participate in higher-resistance objectives; 6. manage Miasma generated by seasonal combat; 7. participate in Blood Moon and Oni King escalation phases. For most players, seasonal resistance progression matters more than simply adding more raw formation CP when a resistance wall is blocking content. Seasonal resources Community references consistently identify: - Stone — a seasonal building resource; - Quartz — produced through Quartz Factories and used for advanced seasonal progression; - event currencies/items such as Magatama or Omamori during specific activities. Exact costs, production rates and shop values are intentionally not frozen in this overview because public tables are version-sensitive. Blood Moon and seasonal enemies Official patch history confirms the following Sealed Island entities/systems: - Rotting Oni ; - Booze Brute ; - Blood Moon Rotting Oni ; - Blood Moon Booze Brute ; - Oni King ; - Blood Moon Shroud ; - Miasma Bursts Alert . The developers changed recommended CP, Viral Resistance and Oni King HP after launch. That makes dated verification essential for any numeric guide. Official balance changes worth remembering In the November 2025 update, the developers: - lowered recommended CP for Lv.1–65 Rotting Onis and Booze Brutes; - reduced Viral Resistance requirements for Lv.65+ Blood Moon variants; - increased Oni King HP because it was dying before enough survivors could participate. A later update also changed the Sealed Island interface during Miasma Bursts Alert , replacing the normal Miasma icon with an Oni King Statue icon. Side events Community sources document additional Sealed Island activities such as: - Sacred Tree Blessing ; - Float Parade ; - seasonal shop/currency cycles; - Miasma-related achievements; - smaller mini-events. These activities are included in the Wiki, but any exact reward table remains provisional until verified against the current Server 504 event UI. Server 504 operational boundary The Game Wiki explains how the game mechanic works . Server-specific policy — city assignments, war windows, alliance responsibilities, territory rules, diplomacy or shared-resource decisions — belongs in the Operational Codex or temporary server notices. Season-number conflict note Some public guides call Sealed Island “Season 5.” Server 504 uses Season 4 — Sealed Island , and the Server 504 Wiki follows the numbering visible in our server context rather than overwriting it with a third-party sequence. en.heading: Oni Seal Hall & Quartz Factory
en.body: Sealed Island — Season Buildings Server 504 naming: Season 4 · Sealed Island Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: Medium-high for building roles; exact upgrade costs remain community-derived and should be verified in-game. Sealed Island progression is gated less by normal shelter CP than by its temporary seasonal systems. The two most important personal progression structures are the Oni Seal Hall and Quartz Factory . Oni Seal Hall The Oni Seal Hall is the core resistance building for Sealed Island. Community guides consistently identify it as the primary way to raise Virus Resistance , which determines how efficiently troops can fight infected seasonal enemies and participate in higher-resistance seasonal objectives. Practical priority: 1. keep the Oni Seal Hall moving before chasing optional seasonal upgrades; 2. compare your current Virus Resistance with the requirement shown on the target before attacking; 3. avoid spending Quartz in ways that delay the next resistance breakpoint. The exact resistance gained per level and upgrade costs can change between season versions, so the Server 504 Wiki should not freeze an old cost table without screenshots from the current season. Quartz Factory Quartz Factories produce Quartz , a major upgrade resource for advanced seasonal structures, especially the Oni Seal Hall. Community guides describe a seasonal resource loop in which: - Stone is used to establish or develop Quartz-producing structures; - Quartz is generated over time and then spent on higher-tier seasonal progression; - additional Quartz sources can appear in missions, passes, shops or event rewards. Official patch notes later mentioned that Sealed Island received more Mints , confirming that the season's economy has been adjusted after launch. That is another reason resource tables should be versioned. Recommended Server 504 planning fields When we capture current in-game values, this article should gain a table containing: - building level; - Quartz cost; - Stone cost; - base build time; - Virus Resistance gained; - Quartz production per hour; - maximum number of Quartz Factories; - pass/VIP bonuses that affect production or factory count. Data-quality warning Several public guides label Sealed Island as a different season number from Server 504. The mechanics are still useful, but Server 504's in-game season numbering takes priority . Numeric building data should be verified from the current Server 504 interface before publication as canonical. en.heading: Miasma & Virus Resistance
en.body: Miasma & Virus Resistance Server 504 naming: Season 4 · Sealed Island Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for the existence of Virus Resistance, Miasma and official balance changes; medium for community-derived stack thresholds. Virus Resistance is the main seasonal combat gate in Sealed Island. Miasma is the infection/penalty system that interacts with seasonal combat and shelter status. Virus Resistance When your Virus Resistance is below the requirement shown for a seasonal target, combat efficiency drops. Community guides describe reduced damage and increased infection risk when attacking under the recommended resistance. Official patch history confirms that the developers actively rebalance this layer. In November 2025 they: - reduced the Viral Resistance requirement of Lv.65+ Blood Moon Rotting Onis ; - reduced the Viral Resistance requirement of Lv.65+ Blood Moon Booze Brutes . Therefore, old resistance charts must not be treated as permanent. Where resistance comes from The Oni Seal Hall is the main seasonal building associated with Virus Resistance in community references. Progressing it is usually more important than chasing raw CP when a resistance wall blocks new enemies or territory objectives. Miasma infection Community guides consistently describe Miasma as a stack-based infection system. Sources report that: - combat can add Miasma stacks; - infected troops/shelters can suffer increasing penalties; - alliance members can help with purification; - natural purification also occurs over time; - high stack counts can trigger severe shelter consequences. Some guides publish exact thresholds such as 20/40/100 stacks and a destruction/teleport cycle. Those numbers are useful as a reference but are not yet promoted to Server 504 canonical data because they are not confirmed by official patch notes available to us. Miasma Bursts Alert Official January patch notes confirm a Miasma Bursts Alert phase in Sealed Island. During this phase, the normal Miasma icon can be replaced by the Oni King Statue icon in the upper-left interface. This confirms that Miasma is not only a passive debuff system; it also has scheduled/event-phase behavior. Practical play Before fighting a new seasonal target: 1. check its Virus Resistance recommendation; 2. compare it with your current resistance; 3. upgrade Oni Seal Hall if the resistance gap is large; 4. monitor Miasma after repeated fights; 5. coordinate purification with alliance members when needed. Do not use raw CP alone to judge whether a seasonal target is efficient to fight. What still needs Server 504 capture - exact damage penalty by resistance deficit; - exact stack thresholds and penalties; - purification amount and cooldown; - natural purification rate; - shelter-destruction/teleport rule at maximum stacks; - achievement thresholds tied to Miasma. Sources - Apple App Store version history — official Sealed Island balance notes and Miasma Bursts Alert: - Community Miasma/Virus guide: - Community Sealed Island guide:

en.heading: Blood Moon Shroud
en.body: Blood Moon Shroud Server 504 naming: Season 4 · Sealed Island Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for event existence and official conflict handling; medium for community reward/currency details. Official patch notes explicitly reference Blood Moon versions of both Rotting Oni and Booze Brute , and later added a warning when Zombie Siege overlaps with Blood Moon Shroud. What changes during Blood Moon Community references describe Blood Moon as an escalation phase where stronger corrupted targets appear and seasonal currencies/rewards become available. Event conflict handling Official October 2025 notes added a secondary confirmation prompt when Zombie Siege conflicts with Blood Moon Shroud . Operationally, this means alliance leadership should avoid assuming both events can be run casually at the same time. When schedules overlap, players may need a clear priority announcement. Magatama and exchange content Community guides associate Blood Moon activity with Magatama and a limited exchange shop often referred to as Lan's Shadow Shop . They also report Rotting Oni and Booze Brute as major sources of this seasonal currency. Because shop stock, costs and reset behavior can change, the Server 504 Wiki should treat any exact exchange table as a dated snapshot rather than a permanent list. Practical checklist Before Blood Moon Shroud: - confirm your Virus Resistance; - prepare stamina/AP if needed for repeated monster hunting; - check alliance rally timing for Booze Brutes; - verify whether another alliance event overlaps; - review the active seasonal shop before spending Magatama; - avoid carrying large amounts of event-only currency into the final phase without checking expiry rules. en.heading: Rotting Oni & Booze Brute
en.body: Rotting Oni & Booze Brute Server 504 naming: Season 4 · Sealed Island Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for official enemy names and balance changes; medium for community descriptions of solo/rally roles and drops. Rotting Oni and Booze Brute are the main recurring infected enemy types associated with Sealed Island's Miasma and Blood Moon systems. Rotting Oni Community guides consistently describe Rotting Oni as the more regular world-map seasonal hunting target. Its practical role is similar to a solo-progression enemy: clear levels, obtain seasonal rewards and move up as Virus Resistance improves. Booze Brute Booze Brute is described by community guides as the larger, rally-oriented seasonal target. Alliance participation therefore matters more than isolated player power. Official balance history The November 2025 official update confirms that these targets were actively tuned: - recommended CP for Lv.1–65 Rotting Onis was lowered; - recommended CP for Lv.1–65 Booze Brutes was lowered; - Viral Resistance requirements for Lv.65+ Blood Moon Rotting Onis were reduced; - Viral Resistance requirements for Lv.65+ Blood Moon Booze Brutes were reduced. This is strong evidence that old CP/resistance charts can become obsolete even during the same season. Normal vs Blood Moon versions The game distinguishes ordinary seasonal targets from Blood Moon variants. The Blood Moon versions should be documented separately when Server 504 captures their current: - CP recommendation; - Virus Resistance requirement; - stamina/AP cost; - rally requirement; - reward pool; - Magatama or other seasonal currency drops. Practical hunting rule Do not judge these monsters only by the recommended CP number. For Sealed Island, a player with enough raw CP but insufficient Virus Resistance can still perform inefficiently. A useful order of checks is: 1. Virus Resistance; 2. current formation strength; 3. target level/version; 4. whether it is a normal or Blood Moon target; 5. whether the target is intended for solo or rally play. Server 504 data target For a future exact table, capture at least five levels across the current accessible range and record both normal and Blood Moon variants. That will let us infer whether scaling is linear or bracketed without relying on outdated public charts. en.heading: Oni King
en.body: Oni King Server 504 naming: Season 4 · Sealed Island Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: High for official boss existence and HP rebalance; medium for community phase/lore details. The Oni King is the major boss encounter associated with Sealed Island's late-season escalation. Official balance history Official November 2025 patch notes state that the Oni King's HP was increased because some servers defeated it too quickly for other survivors to participate. The developers explicitly said the goal was to extend participation time without increasing encounter difficulty . This distinction matters: - boss HP can change; - boss difficulty does not necessarily change at the same time; - old kill-time expectations therefore become unreliable after a patch. Miasma Bursts connection A later official patch confirms that during the Miasma Bursts Alert phase, the Miasma icon in the top-left interface can be replaced by the Oni King Statue icon. That indicates a direct UI/event-state connection between Miasma escalation and Oni King activity. Practical alliance preparation Before the Oni King phase: 1. announce the expected start time in server time; 2. make sure players have sufficient Virus Resistance for the active phase; 3. keep strongest rally leads available; 4. avoid unnecessary troop commitments immediately before the boss window; 5. coordinate participation so the boss is not burned down before late arrivals can score if participation rewards matter; 6. verify any personal attack-count, damage-ranking or milestone rules in the current event UI. What not to publish as permanent truth Do not hard-code: - Oni King HP; - recommended CP; - Virus Resistance requirement; - number of attempts; - damage milestones; - ranking reward values. Official patch history already proves the boss HP was changed after launch. Community naming note Some guides connect the Oni King to Shuten-dōji / Shuten-doom terminology. These names are useful for finding community guides, but the Server 504 Wiki should prefer names visible in the current Dark War: Survival UI when documenting mechanics. en.heading: Sacred Tree Blessing
en.body: Sacred Tree Blessing Server 504 naming: Season 4 · Sealed Island Last verified: 7 Aug 2026 Source confidence: Medium. The event is documented consistently by Sealed Island community guides and has been observed in Server 504 seasonal context, but the exact reward/buff table is not confirmed by accessible official patch notes. Sacred Tree Blessing is a Sealed Island seasonal activity built around collective contribution rather than direct PvP combat. Community references describe players contributing a seasonal prayer item, commonly called Omamori , to advance a shared blessing meter associated with the Sacred Tree. Core idea The event should be understood as a contribution cycle: 1. obtain the active contribution item through seasonal activities; 2. contribute it to the Sacred Tree event; 3. advance personal and/or collective progress; 4. unlock milestone rewards or temporary season benefits when thresholds are reached. Community guides also describe alliance-level effects such as temporary buffs or purification support, but the exact implementation should be verified from the current Server 504 event panel before being listed as canonical. Omamori Community sources identify Omamori as the contribution item used in Sacred Tree-related activities. They also warn that seasonal items can expire at the end of the season. Because Sealed Island contains multiple event currencies and temporary items, players should check the item description before hoarding it for later weeks. Practical planning When Sacred Tree Blessing is active: - check whether contribution rewards have personal and alliance tracks; - avoid spending the contribution item elsewhere until current event priorities are clear; - coordinate alliance announcements if a shared threshold needs concentrated contributions; - claim milestone rewards before the event phase closes; - verify whether unused Omamori carries into the next phase or expires at season end. What still needs Server 504 capture - exact event duration; - exact Omamori acquisition sources; - contribution amount per action; - personal milestone rewards; - alliance milestone rewards; - exact blessing buffs and duration; - whether the meter is alliance-wide, server-wide or individual + collective; - expiry rules for unused contribution items. en.heading: World Map & State Systems
en.body: World Map & State Systems Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Scope: World-map movement, shelter defense, cross-state interaction and State-level systems. Rule: Season-specific mechanics are versioned and are not treated as permanent global rules. Dark War: Survival's world map connects several systems that are easy to confuse if read separately: scouting, teleportation, shelter defense, durability, gathering, special map structures, cross-state combat and State administration. Core map layers Movement & information - Radar and scouting provide map intelligence. - March queues are used for attacks, rallies, gathering and scouting. - Auto Return behavior differs by activity; current official notes say it is enabled by default for solo-zombie attacks and disabled by default for other march scenarios. Shelter defense - Peace Shields protect shelters from hostile interaction while active. - The City Gate manages defense squads. - Current official client behavior supports multiple Defense Presets. - Shelter durability and burning matter independently from troop casualties. Cross-state warfare Current official rules allow direct destination selection during supported cross-state events rather than random relocation. The opposing State map can be tapped directly during events such as State of Supremacy and Alliance Duel Enemy Buster. The former Capital Teleporter is being phased out: Advanced Teleporters can now be used in the Lost Lands, while remaining Capital Teleporters are consumed first if a player still owns them. Special map zones Some structures create unusual combat conditions. Trade Post / Merchant Guild dark zones, Capital Lost Lands, Mutant Mines and season maps can all alter attack, teleport, mortality or durability behavior. State-level layer The State system includes the President, Presidential Palace officials, State-wide events and cross-state rules. Older community guides describe broad President powers, while current official patches continue to modify the Officials interface and term rewards. Wiki boundary This article describes what the game permits . Server 504 agreements about who may attack, rotate Capital, use Armories, coordinate cross-state movement or appoint representatives belong in the Server Charter / Operational Codex instead. en.heading: Peace Shields & Shelter Defense
en.body: Peace Shields & Shelter Defense Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Confidence: High for current map/UI behavior; exact shield durations and item inventory remain version-sensitive. Peace Shields are the primary shelter-protection tool on the world map. They should be understood together with City Gate defense, shelter durability and event-specific attack rules. Current confirmed behavior Official patch history confirms that Peace Shield status remains visible on shelters even after zooming the world map. This matters for target selection during busy war periods. The Alliance Shop currently sells Advanced Teleporters and historically has also been a common source of Peace Shields. Exact shield stock, duration and purchase limits should be checked against the live Server 504 shop rather than copied from an older guide. Defense is more than a shield A shield prevents hostile interaction while valid, but an unshielded shelter still has several defensive layers: - City Gate defense squads; - hero and troop formation quality; - reinforcements where allowed; - Hospital capacity; - Warehouse-protected resources; - shelter durability. Community building data describes the Warehouse as protecting a portion of Wood, Iron, Power and Coin from plunder. That is economic protection, not battle immunity. Event exceptions Do not assume ordinary shelter rules remain unchanged inside special war zones. Trade Post / Merchant Guild dark zones, battlefield maps, Capital Lost Lands and seasonal areas can modify mortality, durability damage or attack restrictions. Official updates have also tested event-day buffs that reduce losses from attacking shelters. Such buffs are explicitly version/event dependent and should never be treated as permanent PvP rules. Safe operational rule Before dropping a shield, check four separate things: 1. whether your shelter can legally be attacked in the current event; 2. City Gate Defense Presets; 3. Hospital capacity; 4. whether your map position has special-zone modifiers. Verification needed Server 504 screenshots should eventually lock: - currently available Peace Shield durations; - exact Alliance/VIP shop price and weekly limits; - shield-breaking actions and warning text; - any event-specific shield restrictions. en.heading: Teleport & Cross-State Movement
en.body: Teleport & Cross-State Movement Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Confidence: High for official current cross-state teleport behavior. Teleport rules changed materially after launch, so older guides can be misleading. Current cross-state model Official patch history states that, during supported cross-state events: - teleporting no longer sends the survivor to a random location in the target State; - the destination can be chosen directly; - the opponent State map can be tapped to teleport during events such as State of Supremacy and Alliance Duel — Enemy Buster ; - Advanced Teleporters can be used inside the Lost Lands around the Capital; - the old Capital Teleporter has been removed from the Alliance Shop; - if a survivor still owns Capital Teleporters, those are consumed before Advanced Teleporters when entering the Lost Lands. Current world-map name colors Official patches also changed map identification during cross-state activity: - survivors from other States visible inside your Home State appear in red; - during State of Supremacy, same-State troops/names are shown in yellow; - other alliances from your own State may also use yellow in supported cross-state contexts; - survivors not participating as the cross-state opponent can appear white. Because these color rules have been revised more than once, use them as UI guidance rather than as a diplomacy rule. Same-State protection during State of Supremacy Current official State of Supremacy rules prevent attacks on other survivors from the same State during the event, reducing accidental friendly attacks. Season-specific teleport rules Conquest seasons can override ordinary movement. In Origin Lands, for example, official patches added teleporting onto tiles owned by the same camp/alliance and preserved tile ownership beneath the relocated shelter. These rules must remain tagged to their season. Advanced Teleporter planning The Alliance Shop weekly limit for Advanced Teleporters was officially increased from 1 to 4 in a 2026 patch. Shop values can change again, so the live shop remains the source of truth. en.heading: City Gate, Durability & Shelter Attacks
en.body: City Gate, Durability & Shelter Attacks Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Confidence: High for current Defense Preset and official durability changes; exact shelter durability values require in-game verification. Shelter defense has two different failure layers: the fighting formation and shelter durability . Winning or losing troop combat is not the same thing as burning down a shelter's wall. City Gate defense Current official patches introduced Defense Preset on the City Gate screen. Survivors can pre-set multiple defense squads. If heroes in the highest-priority preset are busy elsewhere, the next preset can be used automatically. If no secondary preset exists, the game can auto-deploy the strongest available heroes. A later official patch added another restriction: when multiple defense squads are configured, one hero can only belong to one defense squad at a time . Durability and Destruction Value Official October 2025 balance notes substantially changed world-building destruction: - Watchtower durability restoration cooldown: 5 min → 60 min ; - solo attack Basic Destruction Value: 3,000 → 6,000 ; - rally attack Basic Destruction Value: 3,000 → 18,000 . At the same time, certain event-specific destruction bonuses were reduced to offset the stronger base values. Those numbers are important historical/current reference points, but shelter, Watchtower, city and season-object durability are separate systems and should not be merged into one generic formula. Shelter burning Official patches explicitly improved burning visual effects as City Wall durability decreases. That confirms durability loss is a persistent map-state mechanic independent from the immediate battle report. Special-zone danger Shelters inside Trade Post / Merchant Guild dark zones can receive much higher durability pressure than ordinary map positions. See the dedicated dark-zone article before evaluating risk based only on troop strength. Operational checklist before war - configure at least one valid Defense Preset; - ensure critical heroes are not all locked in incompatible activities; - check Hospital capacity; - know whether the shelter is in a special combat zone; - distinguish troop losses from durability damage in reports and map state. Verification needed Server 504 captures can improve this page with: - current City Gate level effects; - exact shelter maximum durability / recovery speed; - fire-state thresholds; - relocation behavior after durability reaches zero; - current defense-preset slot limits. Sources - Apple App Store — Defense Preset: - Apple App Store — hero uniqueness across defense squads: - Apple App Store — Durability & Destruction Value changes:

en.heading: Trade Post & Merchant Guild Dark Zones
en.body: Trade Post & Merchant Guild Dark Zones Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Confidence: High for official dark-zone combat modifiers; broader structure ownership/economy mechanics still need current capture. Trade Post and Merchant Guild areas can create dark zones where shelter combat behaves differently from ordinary world-map attacks. Official dark-zone combat modifiers A December 2025 official patch changed shelter attacks inside a Trade Post / Merchant Guild dark zone: - attacking-troop mortality rate: 20% → 10% ; - defending troops receive an additional +4% mortality rate ; - shelter durability reduction multiplier was increased by 500% . This means a shelter that looks defensible by normal-map standards may be much more vulnerable to durability pressure inside one of these zones. Why positioning matters The relevant lesson is not simply "attackers are safer." Dark-zone combat changes several loss channels at the same time: 1. attacker mortality; 2. defender mortality; 3. shelter durability damage. Always identify the map zone before comparing two battle reports. Interaction with world battles Current official client controls allow troops to be dragged directly onto world-map targets including Merchant Guild structures. The exact interaction options depend on the current event/season state. What is not yet canonical The public patch history confirms dark-zone combat modifiers, but it does not provide a complete current specification for: - who may occupy/control each Trade Post / Merchant Guild; - reward cadence; - structure level progression; - dark-zone radius; - all capture conditions; - whether those values vary by season/state progression. Those fields should be filled from Server 504 in-game screenshots, not inferred from the dark-zone patch alone. en.heading: Mutant Mines
en.body: Mutant Mines Last verified: 8 Aug 2026 Confidence: Historical community capture only; exact schedule, teleport count and reward caps must be checked against the active Server 504 event. Mutant Mines are a cross-state resource-control activity documented in an older community guide. The mechanic is useful for understanding how map resource systems can temporarily override normal State boundaries, but the original public source is no longer treated as a live authority. Historically documented event loop The archived community description recorded Mutant Mines in the Back Zone as being protected by high virus concentration except during recurring sandstorm windows . During those windows, survivors could cross into States in the same season group and contest the mines. The historical guide listed three daily windows at: - 01:00 server time; - 10:00 server time; - 19:00 server time; with each reduced-virus window lasting one hour. These times are preserved only as investigation targets. Server 504 should verify the live event Rules page before publishing them as current. Resources The historical community description says captured Mutant Mines continuously generated: - Antigens ; - Crimson Ores . Collection also contributed alliance gathering points. The same guide said personal resource collection had a daily cap while alliance gathering-point contribution did not. Cross-state movement The archived description recorded 3 free cross-state teleport chances per day during active Mutant Mine periods. This value is not current-canonical until reconfirmed in game. It also belongs specifically to the Mutant Mines event and must not be generalized to State of Supremacy or other cross-state systems. Combat restrictions Historical community documentation said cross-state survivors could not attack Watchtowers outside the Lost Lands and their own Watchtowers were likewise protected, while the Lost Lands / Capital area removed that restriction. Treat this as event-specific and unverified until reconfirmed in the current Rules panel. Strategy layer Mutant Mines combine three different objectives: 1. secure an active-window position; 2. capture or hold productive mines; 3. convert personal gathering into alliance ranking contribution. A strong alliance plan therefore needs both combat groups and collection uptime rather than treating the activity as pure PvP. Verification needed Capture the active Server 504 event Rules page for: - current sandstorm windows; - free teleport count; - daily Antigen / Crimson Ore caps; - alliance ranking formula; - Watchtower attack restrictions; - mine tiers and production rates. en.heading: Research Center — Overview
en.body: Research Center — Overview Last verified: 2026-08-08 Confidence: Official system identity + community structure data The Research Center is the shelter building used for technology progression. Research is one of Dark War: Survival's main permanent account-growth systems because it improves economic efficiency, development speed, troop performance and event-specific scoring. What the Research Center does Public current-era sources consistently show several research families: - Development — account infrastructure, queues, capacity and efficiency. - Economy — gathering and resource production. - Battle — troop/faction combat improvements. - Duel Research — Alliance Duel scoring and reward efficiency. - Battle Strategy — late competitive combat progression that consumes Wisdom Medals. The exact tree layout, prerequisites and costs are version-sensitive. The Wiki therefore treats tree names and confirmed effects as stable reference, while exact node cost tables remain subject to Server 504 verification. Building progression Community structure data places the Research Center unlock around Watchtower Lv.8 and shows the building increasing Research Speed as it levels. A Fandom structure table lists a progression from roughly +0.1% at Lv.1 to +3.0% at Lv.30 , but this is community-maintained data and should not be treated as a current official cost/effect table without in-game confirmation. The Research Center also appears repeatedly as a Watchtower prerequisite at higher progression stages, which makes it both a technology building and a shelter-progression gate. Why research planning matters Research consumes several distinct resources depending on the tree: - ordinary resources and Research Speedups; - Wisdom Medals for advanced Duel / Battle Strategy progression; - time, which can often be more limiting than resources; - event timing, because Research CP, Research Speedups and Wisdom Medal consumption can all become scoring actions. This is why a good account does not simply research the shortest available node. It chooses a node whose permanent value and event timing justify the cost. Current high-confidence patch note Official 2026 patch history explicitly references: Research Center → Battle Strategy → Kill Training and states that Kill Training technologies take effect on War Days Wednesday & Saturday during the Origin Lands season. This confirms Battle Strategy is an actively maintained live research branch, not only legacy community terminology. Data quality rule The Wiki will publish exact research costs only when one of these conditions is met: 1. current Server 504 screenshots show the node and cost; 2. current official patch notes state the value; or 3. multiple current sources agree and the value is clearly version-labeled. Old full-tree screenshots are useful for discovery, but not enough to overwrite current in-game UI. en.heading: Development & Economy Research
en.body: Development & Economy Research Last verified: 2026-08-08 Confidence: Community-backed structure; exact node values pending current UI capture Development and Economy research improve the account's underlying efficiency rather than directly winning one battle. Their value compounds because construction, research, training, gathering and healing happen continuously. Development research Current community guides place systems such as the following under the broader Development path: - formation / march availability; - construction efficiency; - research efficiency; - training-related capacity or speed; - hospital-related capacity or recovery efficiency; - other shelter-wide throughput improvements. One frequently cited recommendation is to unlock additional Formations early because more simultaneous marches improve gathering, rallies and map activity. The exact node name, level requirement and costs should be checked in the current Research Center UI before being entered as canonical. Economy research Economy research generally focuses on: - gathering speed; - resource-production efficiency; - resource-specific gathering or production bonuses; - long-term farming throughput. Economy nodes often look less impressive than direct combat CP, but they improve the rate at which future buildings, technologies and troop training can be funded. Development vs Economy: which first? A practical priority rule is: 1. remove a hard bottleneck first — formation count, research throughput, training capacity, hospital capacity; 2. take high-frequency efficiency bonuses next — research/construction/gathering speed; 3. fill resource-specific economy nodes when they solve a real bottleneck; 4. do not delay essential Duel or Battle Strategy milestones only to complete low-impact economy nodes. Event timing Research completion can overlap with recurring event scoring. Survival Preparedness has historically included: - Tech CP gained; - Wisdom Medals consumed; - Research Speedups consumed. Exact point values can change and should be checked on the active event page. The permanent rule is simpler: if an upgrade is not urgently needed, completing or claiming it during a matching scoring window can create extra value from the same research investment. Industrial-stage note Industrial accounts often stop being limited purely by Wood/Iron/Electricity and become constrained by specialized materials, long timers and late research requirements. That changes priority from "finish the cheapest node" to "protect scarce resources for the branch that unlocks the next meaningful account milestone." The Wiki does not yet have a verified complete Industrial Research tree. Exact late-game node costs remain in the verification queue. Avoid these mistakes - researching low-impact economy nodes while a major formation/queue bottleneck is still open; - spending all Research Speedups outside scoring windows for non-urgent nodes; - assuming older tech screenshots still match the current tree; - treating raw Research CP as more important than the effect unlocked. en.heading: Battle & Faction Research
en.body: Battle & Faction Research Last verified: 2026-08-08 Confidence: Community-backed branch structure; exact node values pending current UI capture Battle research converts account progression into direct troop performance. Unlike Development and Economy, these technologies are usually judged by how much they improve the formation you actually field. Core combat dimensions Public community references consistently describe Battle research around improvements such as: - troop ATK; - troop DEF; - troop HP; - troop capacity / expansion; - Fighter-specific bonuses; - Rider-specific bonuses; - Shooter-specific bonuses; - other combat modifiers unlocked deeper in the tree. The exact current node order and level caps are not yet published as canonical on this Wiki. Main-faction logic Research should generally reinforce the faction and formation you use most often rather than spreading equally across every troop type from the beginning. A practical sequence is: 1. universal troop-capacity or broad combat improvements; 2. the primary faction used by your strongest formation; 3. secondary formation support; 4. off-faction completion later when the cost is justified. This does not mean faction research should ignore the counter system. Fighter, Rider and Shooter still interact through faction counters, so broad account strength eventually matters. The priority question is simply where the next scarce research resource creates the most immediate value. Troop Expansion Current 2026 community strategy guides repeatedly identify Troop Expansion as a high-value early Battle target because formation capacity improves the number of units benefiting from every other stat bonus. This is a strategy recommendation, not an official universal "best node" rule. Its value depends on current capacity, hero formation, troop tier and research cost. Research CP is not combat efficiency Two technologies with similar CP gain can have very different practical effects. Evaluate Battle research using: - actual main-squad stat affected; - whether the effect applies to all troops or one faction; - prerequisite cost; - research time; - whether it unlocks a deeper key node; - whether the research can be timed with a scoring event. Relationship to Battle Strategy Do not confuse the ordinary Battle tree with Battle Strategy . Battle Strategy is a separate advanced Wisdom Medal-gated system used for competitive combat/event progression. Official 2026 patch history explicitly references Research Center → Battle Strategy → Kill Training . See Battle Strategy & Kill Training /wiki/battle-strategy-and-kill-training . Verification needs To build a current numeric Battle tree, Server 504 captures should include: - full node names; - prerequisite arrows; - max levels; - faction affected; - effect per level; - resource/Wisdom Medal requirements if any; - research time. en.heading: Duel Research
en.body: Duel Research Last verified: 2026-08-08 Confidence: Strong community consensus; exact costs and unlock requirements remain version-sensitive Duel Research is the Alliance Duel-focused technology tree that improves how efficiently an account converts normal weekly activity into Alliance Duel points and rewards. This tree is strategically unusual because improving it can increase the rate at which you earn the Wisdom Medals required for further advanced research. Frequently documented key nodes Current community guides repeatedly reference the following Duel technologies: - Incentive Gathering — increases points from gathering-related Duel tasks. - Incentive Zombies — increases points from zombie-related Duel tasks. - Victory Tycoon — broad Alliance Duel point multiplier. - Richer Rewards I and Richer Rewards II — unlock additional personal milestone reward chests. - One More — increases reward output at the end of the tree. These names are strongly corroborated by multiple current community references, but exact percentages, prerequisite levels and Wisdom Medal costs should be read from the current in-game tree before being treated as Server 504 canonical data. Why Duel Research is often prioritized The value loop is: Duel Research → easier/higher Alliance Duel scoring → more milestone rewards → more Wisdom Medals → faster advanced research For that reason, current community strategy generally recommends completing the important Duel multipliers before diverting a large Wisdom Medal reserve into Battle Strategy. That recommendation is an optimization framework, not an official requirement. A combat-focused account may intentionally accept slower Duel progression to reach a critical Battle Strategy node. Be careful with old cost tables Public reports show that Duel Research costs and presentation have changed across server generations. There are even player reports of different Richer Rewards paths/costs being visible in different interfaces on newer servers. Because of this, the Wiki does not publish one historic Richer Rewards or One More cost as universal. Practical sequence For a normal progressing account: 1. identify the next node that directly improves a recurring Duel theme; 2. prioritize milestone-unlock nodes such as Richer Rewards when reachable; 3. protect enough Wisdom Medals to avoid stalling immediately before a major node; 4. consume Medals during a matching event window when the timing is not urgent; 5. only shift heavily into Battle Strategy after the desired Duel efficiency layer is established. Alliance Duel changes can affect tree value Official patches continue to change Alliance Duel itself — including Enemy Buster scheduling, Pet-item scoring and season-specific point acquisition. Therefore a Duel node's practical importance can change even when the node itself is unchanged. Verification queue Still needed from Server 504: - complete current Duel tree screenshot; - exact node prerequisites; - exact Wisdom Medal costs by level; - current Richer Rewards I/II unlock effects; - current One More effect wording; - current point multiplier values. en.heading: Battle Strategy & Kill Training
en.body: Battle Strategy & Kill Training Last verified: 2026-08-08 Confidence: Official branch existence + current patch behavior; detailed node tree pending UI capture Battle Strategy is an advanced Research Center branch associated with Wisdom Medal progression and competitive combat. It should not be confused with the ordinary Battle research tree. Official current confirmation Dark War: Survival's 2026 official patch history explicitly names: Research Center → Battle Strategy → Kill Training and states that Kill Training technologies take effect on War Days — Wednesday and Saturday — during the Origin Lands season . This is important for two reasons: 1. Battle Strategy remains an actively maintained live system. 2. Some Battle Strategy effects can depend on event/season context rather than being permanently active everywhere. What Battle Strategy is for Current community references describe Battle Strategy as a Wisdom Medal-gated combat progression path that becomes especially important after the account has established its Duel Research economy. Exact branches may include troop combat, kill-event or war-day effects, but the Wiki will not reconstruct the full tree from screenshots or memory without current evidence. Kill Training The official patch gives one current behavior rule: - during Origin Lands , Kill Training technologies apply on War Days Wednesday & Saturday . Do not extrapolate that statement into a universal all-season rule. Outside Origin Lands, or after future season changes, the active window may differ. Duel Research vs Battle Strategy A useful decision framework: Duel Research improves recurring reward/point efficiency. Battle Strategy spends the same scarce Wisdom Medal pool toward combat-oriented progression. This creates an opportunity-cost problem. Community strategy usually recommends establishing the important Duel efficiency nodes first because they improve future Wisdom Medal income, then investing more aggressively into Battle Strategy. However, an account preparing for a major competitive war may rationally prioritize a high-impact Battle Strategy breakpoint sooner. What must be verified Server 504 captures are needed for: - full Battle Strategy tree; - Kill Training node names and levels; - exact effects; - Wisdom Medal costs; - Gold/resource costs if applicable; - prerequisite nodes; - which effects are permanent vs war-day/season conditional. Source policy Official patch text controls current conditional behavior. Community guides are useful for strategic sequencing, but cannot define exact current Kill Training values. en.heading: Wisdom Medals
en.body: Wisdom Medals Last verified: 2026-08-08 Confidence: High for purpose/sources; exact event point values remain version-sensitive Wisdom Medals are a scarce research material used primarily for advanced Duel Research and Battle Strategy progression. Because these trees compete for the same resource pool, Wisdom Medals should be treated as a strategic currency rather than ordinary inventory. Confirmed / strongly supported uses Current community references consistently identify Wisdom Medals as required for: - Duel Research ; - Battle Strategy . Official patch history confirms Battle Strategy as an active current Research Center branch, while current Alliance Shop material descriptions and guides continue to identify Wisdom Medals as the advanced research currency. Recurring sources Current references list sources such as: - Alliance Duel personal milestone rewards; - Alliance Shop; - legacy/current Honor-family shop sources depending rollout and version; - selected event rewards / offers. The exact weekly amount available varies with account progress, Duel Research, shop inventory and event version. Why hoarding can be correct Spending a Wisdom Medal creates two kinds of value: 1. permanent research progression; 2. possible event points if the active theme rewards Medal consumption. Therefore, if the research is not urgent, holding Medals until an overlapping scoring window can produce more total value. Survival Preparedness has historically included Wisdom Medal consumption as a scoring action. Alliance Duel and other events can also make research timing more valuable. Always check the active event page because point values can change. Duel-first logic A common current recommendation is: establish key Duel Research → improve future reward/Medal velocity → invest deeper into Battle Strategy. This is especially sensible when Richer Rewards / One More or other major Duel breakpoints are close. Do not follow this blindly. If a critical combat technology is needed for a major war, Battle Strategy can reasonably take priority. Alliance Shop priority Current 2026 community shop guidance usually ranks Wisdom Medals among the highest-value recurring Alliance Shop purchases after the relevant research trees unlock, because they gate permanent progression and have fewer routine sources than ordinary resources or speedups. Do not confuse with other medals Dark War: Survival contains several medal-like resources. Pet progression, events and other systems can use their own medals/currencies. Spec Ops Honor Medals , for example, belong to Pet Agent progression and are not Wisdom Medals. Verification needed - current Server 504 Alliance Shop price/weekly limit; - current Honor Shop availability if any; - current Duel milestone Medal totals; - exact Medal cost by Duel/Battle Strategy node; - current event scoring per Medal. en.heading: Research Queues, Speed & Timing
en.body: Research Queues, Speed & Timing Last verified: 2026-08-08 Confidence: Strong for timing principles; exact VIP/queue unlock values require current UI verification Research progression is not only about choosing the right technology. It is also about keeping the Research Center active and consuming speedups at the right time. Research Speed The Research Center building itself increases Research Speed as it levels according to community structure data. Additional research-speed effects can also come from account progression, heroes, VIP or technologies depending the current version. Exact stacking formulas are not yet published as canonical on this Wiki. Research queues Community guides report access to an additional research queue through VIP progression and temporary VIP activation strategies. Because exact VIP unlock wording can change, the Wiki does not currently hard-code a specific VIP level as an official rule without a fresh in-game capture. The practical rule remains: an idle research queue is lost progression time. If a second queue is available, use it to separate: - one long-duration strategic research; - one shorter branch-clearing or prerequisite research. Research Speedups Research Speedups are most efficient when they solve one of three problems: 1. reach a meaningful technology breakpoint; 2. free a queue that would otherwise sit blocked; 3. overlap progression with a scoring event. Using large speedup reserves merely to finish a low-impact node immediately is usually poor timing. Claim timing When an event scores Tech CP gained , the exact moment at which progress is recognized matters. Depending on event implementation, completing or claiming an upgrade inside the scoring window can matter more than when the research was started. Before staging long research across reset, verify the active event Rules page rather than assuming the scoring trigger. Double-dip logic The highest-value research window is one where several scoring actions overlap, for example: - Tech CP gained; - Research Speedups consumed; - Wisdom Medals consumed. This is the same principle Server 504 already applies to other save-and-spend systems: preserve non-urgent resources until one action satisfies multiple event objectives. What should never wait Do not delay research purely for event points when the delay blocks: - a Watchtower prerequisite; - a troop-tier unlock; - a key Formation/queue upgrade; - a major Duel Research reward breakpoint; - an essential Battle Strategy technology before war. Permanent progression lost for several days can be worth more than the extra event points. Research-time verification queue Still useful to capture from Server 504: - current second-queue unlock condition; - VIP research bonuses; - current Research Center speed effect by level; - how Tech CP scoring is triggered in active events; - current speedup point values. en.heading: Late-Game & Industrial Research
en.body: Late-Game & Industrial Research Last verified: 2026-08-08 Confidence: Framework-level only; exact late-game tree requires Server 504 capture After Watchtower 30 and the transition into Industrial progression, research planning becomes less about clearing cheap early nodes and more about managing specialized bottlenecks, long timers and combat breakpoints. What changes in late game Early research is often limited by ordinary resources and short prerequisites. Late-game accounts increasingly face: - longer research timers; - larger Gold/resource requirements; - scarce Wisdom Medal decisions; - Industrial building/material bottlenecks; - faction specialization; - event/season-conditional technologies; - higher opportunity cost for every queue slot. Research and Industrial progression are connected Industrial progression already competes for resources such as Precision Parts and other specialized materials. Even when a research node does not directly consume those materials, research timing still competes with construction for: - speedups; - ordinary resources; - event windows; - player attention and queue availability. This is why late-game planning should use a combined construction/research roadmap rather than two independent lists. Late-game priority model Before starting a long technology, ask: 1. Does it unlock a required building/troop/research milestone? 2. Does it materially improve the main war formation? 3. Is it prerequisite tax for a much stronger node? 4. Does it consume Wisdom Medals that are needed for Duel/Battle Strategy elsewhere? 5. Can the completion overlap with Alliance Duel or Survival Preparedness? 6. Will using speedups here delay a higher-value Industrial construction push? Do not publish inferred cost tables Public guides often discuss late-game research broadly, but current full Industrial/advanced tree data is incomplete. The Wiki therefore does not manufacture a cost table from account screenshots of unknown server age. Current official example of late research being season-aware Official 2026 patch history states that Research Center → Battle Strategy → Kill Training technologies apply on Wednesday and Saturday War Days during Origin Lands. That is a strong example of why late-game technology must be documented with scope and season , not just effect value. Server 504 data needed For a true late-game research reference, capture: - every research branch currently visible after WT30; - unlock prerequisites; - node max levels; - Research/Gold/Wisdom Medal costs; - timer per level; - faction/universal scope; - whether effects are permanent, event-only or season-only.
